chapters.title: Welcome
chapters.html:
PS5 Cooling & System Center - Pro is a homebrew program (ELF) for a jailbroken PS5. It controls the fan according to a calm, freely adjustable target temperature and comes with a web interface that you open from any device on your home network: phone, tablet, PC or the console's own browser. On top of that come game management, packages, saved data, a file manager, payloads, profile and system information.

Quiet, not loudThe control holds a target temperature – gently and slowly, without constant ups and downs.
Everything in the browserNo installation on a PC needed: open the address, done.
Internet only on demandOn its own, the app only talks to programs on the console and to the browsers on your home network. It goes onto the internet (GitHub) only when you trigger it: loading the payload list and payloads, fetching a newer version of AMPR EMU NG, Dump Forge or Kraken Mount.
Safe to useAlmost every action works on the first click; only deleting asks first and names what will go. Running games and saved data are protected.
Tested on a PS5 Pro (CFI-7021) with firmware 12.00. Firmware 1.00 to 14.22 is supported (the SDK's start-up code knows it); on the remaining versions the app is not tested, users also report it on 4.xx to 10.xx and 13.60.

chapters.title: Requirements
chapters.html:
• A PS5 with a jailbreak and a loaded payload loader (elfldr, port 9021).
  • Firmware 1.00 to 14.22: The start-up code of the SDK the app is built with knows these versions; on any other version it does not start at all. Only 12.00 is tested.
  • kstuff must be loaded – only with it can the app reach the fan controller. Without kstuff, the display and the web interface work, but fan control then reports “not available”.
  • A device with a browser on the same home network.
  • To send the ELF, a program such as nc (netcat) or a payload sender of your choice.
  • Optional: ShadowMountPlus – it creates the tiles (see “Installation”) and is needed for moving, unpacking, mounting and unmounting, and for safely ejecting USB drives (NTFS drives are ejected by the app itself).

chapters.title: Installation & first start
chapters.html:
1. Send PS5_Cooling_System_Center_v{version}.elf to the console, port 9021, e.g.:
    nc -q0 <PS5-IP> 9021 < PS5_Cooling_System_Center_v{version}.elf
  2. A notification with the address of the web interface appears at the top left of the TV.
  3. Open it in the browser: http://<PS5-IP>:8086/

The tiles

The release contains two tiles. Copy the folder from the zip to /data/homebrew/ (by FTP or with the file manager); ShadowMountPlus then adds the tile.

  • FAKE86921 – Fullscreen: starts the app if it is not running yet and shows it fullscreen with the controller (see “The fullscreen app”).
  • FAKE86922 – Browser: starts the app as well and opens the web interface in the console's browser.
  • Both carry the app in their eboot.bin. After an update, copy the folders from the new release (the fullscreen app must be closed for that). With a tile you no longer need to send the ELF after a restart.
  • An older running app is replaced (since 1.77.1): When you tap a tile, it compares the versions. If an older app is still running – for example because the console was not restarted – the built-in one takes its place (it ends the old one on start; the tile waits up to 30 seconds for that). An equal or newer app stays. If a job is running (packing, copying, installing, save games …), nothing is replaced, because that would cancel the job: the tile reports that a newer app is ready (the message is in German); open it again after the job. Tiles from 1.77.0 or older cannot do this yet – send the new ELF once or restart the console.
Only ever run one instance. Two instances control the fan at the same time and get in each other's way. A newly sent ELF ends an older instance itself; if that does not work, you end the old one on the “Payloads” page, otherwise a restart helps.
With one of the tiles FAKE86921/FAKE86922 the former media tile (PSCC69690) is not needed. If you send only the ELF and have neither of the two tiles, the app creates one itself, once, about a minute after it starts, under “Media” (only if no game is running at that moment). It only opens the web interface and does not start the app; a deleted one does not come back.

chapters.title: The interface at a glance
chapters.html:
On the left is the sidebar with the sections Cooling, Games, File manager, Payloads, System, Profile, Log and Credits (below them the links Manual and FAQ). At the top in the header, on every page: the power options, “Fullscreen” and the connection indicator. “Expert mode” now sits only on the System page and is off by default.

“Fullscreen” hides the browser's taskbar and window frame. In the PS5's own browser the first press on the page switches to fullscreen by itself; on a PC or phone the page stays in a normal window until you press “Fullscreen” (the button remembers it, “Exit fullscreen” turns it off again). Under the “FAQ” entry in the sidebar you find the version of the running app.

Design. Next to the language you choose one of four designs: Standard (dark blue with glowing edges), Light (muted grey-blue, does not dazzle), Dark (almost black, without glow) and Optimal (for the TV and the PS5: strong contrast, larger text, no translucency or shadows, the fastest to draw). Every device remembers its own choice, for example “Optimal” on the TV and “Light” on the phone.

Power options

Rest Mode, Restart, Turn off and Safe Mode. Every command works on the first click; while it runs the button is locked, so a double click does not trigger it twice.

When turning off or restarting, unsaved game progress is lost.

Language

At the top right of the header you choose the language of the interface: Deutsch, English, Italiano, Español, Français, Русский or Svenska. On the first visit (and with the choice “Auto (system)”), the page in the PS5's browser uses the console's language, otherwise your browser's; if that is not available, English. The browser remembers the choice; the page then reloads and stays on the section you were on. Numbers, dates and times follow the language.

Notifications that the console itself shows on the TV (at start or with a warning) are in German.

Manual and FAQ

The entries Manual and FAQ at the bottom of the sidebar open these texts directly in the app, in the chosen language (without the screenshots, so that the app stays small).

Windows and the right stick

When a window opens (e.g. for deleting), the background is dimmed and stays still. In the PS5's browser, the right stick then only scrolls the window itself.

Controller keys

In the console's browser four buttons help: L1 and R1 go to the previous and next page of the sidebar, L2 and R2 scroll the page up and down. The browser reports them to the page as the keys F5 to F8; they do not reload the page.

chapters.title: The fullscreen app
chapters.html:
The tile FAKE86921 shows the app fullscreen on the TV, operated with the controller – no browser at all. It can do almost everything the web interface can; both work with the same running app.

Buttons

  • Touchpad button: opens the sidebar with Cooling, Games, File manager, Payloads, System, Profile and Log.
  • L1 / R1: previous and next area. L2 / R2: the sub-tabs (e.g. Games → Library, Playtime, Packages …).
  • D-pad: select and change values. Cross button: start or confirm, Circle button: back.
  • Square button: actions for the selection (e.g. copy a game, delete a payload, edit a profile), Triangle button: details or “More”.
  • Options button: menu with “Open web interface in the browser”, “Reload”, “Sprache / Language”, “Quit app” and the power options.
  • Language: German, English, Spanish, French, Italian, Russian or Swedish. By default it follows the console’s system language (other languages: English); Options button → “Sprache / Language” opens a list of all languages (tick = active); one press picks one and the choice is kept. Texts no dictionary knows stay German.

The bar at the bottom always shows what the buttons do right now. Quit and cancel act on the first press – there are no confirmation questions. Deleting is the exception: it asks first and names what will go.

Areas

  • Cooling: overview with the target temperature; settings with operating mode, safety limit, fan speed ceiling, warnings, light bar, game profiles, night mode and fan self-test; fan curve with the automatic mode's curve and the control recording.
  • Games: library with an actions menu (copy, convert, move, unpack, check image, delete, extras, unmount and mount, quit the running game), playtime, saves, packages (install, queue, split), PS4 PKG from USB, FPKGMount, disc, backups and jobs.
  • File manager, Payloads (own, already loaded, store, profiles), System (console, ShadowMountPlus, storage, cooling health, extra probes, expert), Profile (name and profile picture, account, thanks) and Log (app log, kernel log live, saved).

What stays in the browser

Uploading files from a PC, downloading files, saving or loading profiles as a file and opening links only work in the web interface. Under System the fullscreen app shows a QR code with its address.

You enter text with the on-screen keyboard; a page of its own has ä, ö, ü and ß. Every area can have its own background picture (System → Storage → Background pictures).

chapters.title: Cooling
chapters.html:
The most important page: the status in plain words, the current temperature, the fan and the running game. Right below, you set the Target temperature and the Operating mode.

{{FIG:01-kuehlung.png}}

Target temperature

The temperature the console should hold: adjustable from 50 to 91 °C, 66 °C by default. Higher means quieter and warmer. Quick select sets the target immediately: Cool 62 °C, Balanced 77 °C, Quiet 91 °C.

91 °C is the value the console sets itself (ShadowMountPlus also offers it as the highest target): the fan stays as quiet as without the app, but the console gets noticeably warmer. The emergency limit is always at least 4 °C above the target (so 95 °C at 91 °C); the app's warning threshold moves with the target (never lower than target + 2 °C), so that it does not warn all the time with a high target; the value set in the settings stays saved.

Operating mode

Quiet, Balanced and Cool determine how strongly the fan responds to heat – they do not change the target. “Quiet” is recommended.

{{FIG:02-kuehlung-betriebsart.png}}

How the control works

  • It works with a moving average, not with single readings.
  • The requested speed follows the fan curve (see below): it already rises gently 10 °C below the target, not only at the target.
  • The trend counts: if the temperature is already falling, the fan is not turned up any further.
  • It turns up in small steps, and turns down only once the temperature has been stably low.
  • Above the safety limit (“Emergency limit” in the advanced settings) all consideration for loudness is dropped and the fan goes quickly to full speed; the firmware always protects itself in addition.

Automatic mode

If “Automatic mode” is off, the app hands control back to the PS5 and only shows values. If the app is not running, the console controls the fan itself again anyway.

Night mode

Below “Target temperature” and “Operating mode” you will find the Night mode card: between two times (for example 23:00 to 07:00) the night target applies instead of the target temperature, usually a warmer and therefore quieter one. A game's own rule takes precedence. The time is the one on the device where you opened the page – the console knows no time zone.

Profiles per game

The Profiles per game card (Cooling, below the temperature history and sensors) switches the target temperature and operating mode by itself as soon as a certain game runs: start the game, set the target and operating mode and press Remember current setting; Remove takes the profile away again. Up to 16 games can be remembered. This requires Game detection under “Extra queries” (System), which is on by default. A game profile takes precedence over night mode. In the fullscreen app it is under Cooling → Settings → Game profiles.

Fan self-test

In the expert view, in the “Fan diagnostics (target / actual / clamp)” card, Test the fan now checks whether the fan responds to the threshold – even without heat. The app briefly lowers the threshold below the temperature and reads the fan speed. If it rises by at least 8 percentage points, the fan responds; otherwise it says “The fan does not respond”. The fan gets audibly louder for up to 30 seconds in the process, and the test only runs when the console is cool.

The console's minimum fan speed

The console never turns the fan below its own minimum value (measured: 20 % at idle, 34 % in a game). The app learns it during operation and shows it in the fan diagnosis; the target/actual deviation is calculated with it.

Display via the mute button

Press the controller's mute button twice quickly: the processor temperature and fan speed appear at the top left (without a sound) – even without the web interface. The microphone is toggled twice in the process and ends up as it was before.

The display is on by default; the switch Display via the mute button in the “Operating mode” card turns it off. It appears at most every 5 seconds.

The fan is shown as a ring, like the temperature: the arc shows the measured value from 0 to 100 % (a full ring is 100 %) and the number sits in the middle. The arc goes from blue through green and yellow to red (grey without a reading).

Pause the game in the background (since 1.86.5)

When a game goes to the background and the home screen is in front, the app pauses the game itself. This protects against an error message from the console (“Device busy”) that could otherwise appear when tapping a tile of the app (browser or full screen): the console pauses a running game the moment a tile is tapped anyway, but fails once in the process, and ShadowMountPlus releases the tile’s mount in the meantime. If the game is already paused, the tile starts at once. For this the app calls the console in a small helper program of its own, only for a real game (never for a tile of the app and never for a media app such as YouTube: only what the Games page lists as a game is paused), only when the home screen itself is in front (not an overlay), only once per stay in the background and only while ShadowMountPlus answers. Right before pausing, the helper checks once more that the home screen is still in front (whoever goes straight back into the game is not paused). The game carries on where it was. The switch Pause the game in the background below the operating mode (on by default) turns it off; the full-screen app has it in its settings.

Fan guard

A second, independent part of the app looks at the temperatures itself every second. If the regulation stays silent for 20 seconds, it hands the fan back to the console – if it is hot, it sets full cooling. If the temperature stays 10 seconds above the safety limit plus 6 °C while the fan is not at full speed, it holds full cooling until it is 8 °C cooler again. If the app crashes, the console gets the fan back. While it steps in, the Cooling page shows “Guard”, and a fixed threshold set by hand is refused.

Fan curve (since 1.86.5)

The Fan curve card (Cooling, under the night mode; in the full-screen app the Fan curve tab) shows as a picture what speed the automatic mode asks for at which temperature – with a dot for the temperature right now. The curve rises gently from 10 °C below the target from the usual minimum speed (23 %), stands at 28 % (Quiet), 33 % (Balanced) or 40 % (Cool) at the target, depending on the mode, and goes on up to full speed, which is reached about 24 °C (Quiet), 17 °C (Balanced) or 14 °C (Cool) above the target. So the fan follows the temperature early and in small steps instead of suddenly spinning up shortly before the target. Only near the safety limit does the control catch up in big steps; otherwise the speed rises slowly (step per second depends on the mode). When a game starts, the first jump of the threshold is damped a little so that the speed does not overshoot.

Ceiling for the fan speed

In normal operation the fan does not go above this speed (30 to 100 %, 100 % = no limit by default). Each mode has its own limit (Quiet 65 %, Balanced 85 %, Cool 100 %); the ceiling can only lower it. It does not apply above the safety limit nor in the fan guard: there the fan runs as high as needed. A low ceiling means a warmer console.

Warning threshold follows the target

In the advanced settings. With the switch on (default), the app's warning threshold rises with the target in automatic mode (never below target + 2 °C). Off: exactly the “Warning from” value applies.

Warning from and emergency limit

Both are in the expert view under “Advanced settings” (in the fullscreen app under Cooling → Settings). Warning from (40 to 110 °C, 80 °C by default) is the processor temperature from which a notification appears on the TV; for the main chip 5 °C more applies automatically. The Emergency limit (72 to 95 °C, 78 °C by default) is the temperature from which the fan goes to full speed regardless of loudness; it is always at least 4 °C above the target. A last resort, not a fine control – best left as it is.

Control recording

The app keeps the last 30 minutes of the control, one line per second: temperatures, what the control asked for, speed, threshold, target, mode. It lives in memory only. In the Fan curve card, Download control recording gives it as a table (CSV); Save on the console puts it in the data folder (in the full-screen app the X button). When the mode or the target changes, the log gets a line.

chapters.title: Games
chapters.html:
The games on your Home screen with cover, format and actions. You can search by title, title ID or content ID; filter by PS5, PS4 or “Backport · AMPR · PlayGo”; and sort by Home screen order, name, play time, size and more. Under “View” you choose large (as before) or compact: in “compact” the cover is small next to the title and the buttons are a row of icons; point at an icon with the mouse or the D-pad (or press “i”) and a bar at the bottom says what it does. The buttons are the same in both views; the browser remembers the choice per device. The firmware the game asks for is shown under the title as well (“FW 13.60”, “PS4-FW” for PS4 titles); if it is newer than the console's and the SDK the game is built with (the eboot.bin's, else the param.json's) is newer as well, the mark is yellow; if the SDK fits the console, it stays grey, because the game starts anyway (since 23 November 2026; the full-screen app shows the row “Built with SDK” in the details). With a backport applied, the firmware the backport carries is shown instead (the SDK version of its eboot.bin); what the param.json asks for is in the tooltip. Since 23 November 2026 also for FPKGMount games: the app reads Kraken Mount's cache for it (eboot.bin and fakelib); the libraries Kraken Mount adds itself (AMPR, PlayGo, DLC) do not count as a backport. Packed (since 17 November 2026): if a game lies in AMPR packs, “zstd packed” or “LZ4 packed” appears under the title, whatever the game’s format (folder or image); “Info & metadata” has the row “Packed”. For images the app reads the two index files (ampr_zstd.index, ampr_assets.index) while it reads the image file, without mounting anything, and remembers it until the file changes; shortly after the app starts the mark may be missing for an image for a moment. In the full-screen app the note is a coloured pill in the game’s row (green: zstd, blue: LZ4) and a row “Packed” in the info panel.

Every card also has Open path: the file manager jumps to the folder in which the game lies (for an image: the image file).

{{FIG:03-spiele-bibliothek.png}}

Starting and closing

  • Start starts the game directly. In the console's browser, the browser closes at once when you tap, before the game loads, so that the game is in front. If the console has something to say (a refusal, an offer “Start”), it shows it as a notification at the top right.
  • If another game is already running, Start closes it and starts the chosen one in one go – anything not saved in the running game is lost. Close game closes the running game immediately.
  • A game is never started twice: a second click does nothing while the first start is under way and for 30 seconds after it.
  • If ShadowMountPlus briefly refuses a start with “Device busy”, the app tries twice more by itself, 3 seconds apart; only then does the notification with “Start” appear (since 1.93.0, also when switching games and in the dump queue).

Mounting and unmounting

On a game's card (full-screen app: Actions), Mount, Remount and Unmount put a game into ShadowMountPlus or take it out (from ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta10) – useful when a game hangs or should be found anew after copying, moving or deleting. Never while the game runs. Important: a game that is mounted but does not run keeps ShadowMountPlus's one place for a mount: as long as it is neither started nor unmounted again, no other game and no tile will start (ShadowMountPlus reports “Device busy”, the console shows a launch error). That is why the Games page shows a yellow notice with an Unmount button (in the full-screen app the row carries the mark MOUNTED), and the message after mounting says it too. If you only wanted the game to be found anew, unmount it afterwards. So that nobody has to unmount anything or wait, the app lets go of a game it mounted itself and nobody started: at once when it starts another game itself; at once when the console refuses another start (the app reads this in the kernel log and says so on the console: then simply try the start again); otherwise after 30 seconds (with a notice on the console; it remembers this across a restart of the app). The 30 seconds only run while no game plays and none of the app's jobs is working. The yellow notice and the mark appear only for games the app mounted itself; a game that ShadowMountPlus or Kraken Mount set up blocks nothing. Whatever the app did not mount, it leaves alone.

The same title at two mounters

Kraken Mount (FPKGMount), ShadowMountPlus and PS4Mount each register every game they find with the console and mount it: all of them write /user/app/<ID> and mount /system_ex/app/<ID>. If the same title ID lies with two of them (for example a .pkg for Kraken Mount and an image or a folder for ShadowMountPlus), they get in each other's way: Kraken Mount takes ShadowMountPlus's mount away, “Device busy” can appear, and the tile differs (Kraken Mount registers the param.json as it is, ShadowMountPlus rewrites it). That is why the FPKGMount tab (browser and full-screen app) shows a yellow caution notice for such a double assignment; the game list has no warning for it. The app moves nothing itself: keep the game at only one of the two. The tab also reports game folders in the search folder of Kraken Mount (FPKG-Games): folder games belong to ShadowMountPlus, only .pkg files should lie in FPKG-Games. Kraken Mount itself has no switch that leaves folders out.

Put FPKG games only in the folder FPKG-Games (internal, M.2 SSD or USB): ShadowMountPlus does not search there. When converting to the format FPKG this folder is therefore preselected (“A · Playable”). If a game nevertheless lies at Kraken Mount and at ShadowMountPlus and is ended, the app unmounts it at ShadowMountPlus (like the “Unmount” button of the card); games that lie at only one of them, and the tiles, stay untouched.

Duplicate images

If a game exists in more than one image on the drives (.exfat, .ffpkg, .ffpfs, .ffpfsc), ShadowMountPlus picks one or the other on each scan. The Games page then shows a Duplicate images card. It starts collapsed; a click on its header opens and closes the list (the state is kept for the session), and “Search again” works while collapsed. The source ShadowMountPlus is using at the moment is marked. Deactivate renames an image to ….off, so ShadowMountPlus no longer takes it; Activate undoes that. Nothing is deleted. A mounted image, or one whose game is running, cannot be deactivated.

The bar above the library shows, besides the app's own jobs, moves, unpacks and – since ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta8 – installations that ShadowMountPlus runs itself (a PKG or a game folder from its own interface, for example); without a title ID it shows the package or file name.

Copying, moving, converting

Dump folders can be copied, moved and converted directly on the console into ffpfsc (compressed, recommended), ffpkg or exFAT – either playable in the folder homebrew of the destination (ShadowMountPlus finds it there) or as a backup in PS5-Sicherung/Spiele. Every copy is read back after writing and verified; nothing is overwritten.

Moving and unpacking are carried out by ShadowMountPlus itself; the app plans the targets and shows the job. When moving, ShadowMountPlus copies the game, registers it at the new place and deletes it at the old one only when everything has arrived; the choice is limited to folders in which ShadowMountPlus itself searches (homebrew, etaHEN/games, on USB and M.2 the root of the drive), so that the game stays playable. You unpack an image in the “Convert” window with Dump folder · extract into a folder with the title ID in the chosen target. A compressed ffpfsc image can only be unpacked (the “Convert” button then opens this window directly); no other format is made from an image: first unpack, then convert the folder. If unpacking ends at ShadowMountPlus with “Permission denied”, the app carries on unpacking the same image itself.

The result is checked afterwards. Thorough (the default) reads it back from the drive once more in full, checks every block and creates <name>.sha256 (not for an image with packs, see below). Quick checks the structure and a sample spread over the whole image (for ffpkg: the structure and all files in one pass instead of two) and creates no checksum file; that saves a lot of time with big games, but a damaged block outside the sample goes unnoticed. With ffpfsc the app stores a block packed only if that saves at least 5 % on it, otherwise raw; this way the console does not have to unpack something for one percent of savings while playing.

Original afterwards (since 18.11.2026). When you convert, copy or unpack, the window asks under “Original afterwards” what is to happen to the original: Keep (the default), Delete or Move. That way the same title does not lie on the console twice – ShadowMountPlus would otherwise report it from two places. Delete asks first and names the game, its size and its path; saved data stays. Move first makes a checked copy (every file read back and compared) in a folder of your choice and deletes the original only after that; you can choose the internal SSD, the M.2 expansion and the USB drives, PS5-Sicherung/Spiele on the chosen drive is suggested, and “Choose folder” opens a small picker. The app refuses a folder in which ShadowMountPlus itself looks for games (homebrew, etaHEN/games, and on USB and M.2 the root down to two levels), as well as one in which something of the same name already exists or that has too little room. The original is deleted or moved only after the job has ended well and its result is there; if it fails or you cancel it, the original stays untouched. If the result was checked only with Quick, the original stays in place with “Delete” (the message says so: then choose “Thorough”); “Move” works even then, because its copy is checked on its own. The app waits until nothing else is running (the queue only after the original of the previous entry); the end arrives as a notification, and the “Original afterwards” line in the window shows the state. For unpacking this replaces the former switch “Delete image afterwards”. The full-screen app offers the same choice.

While the original is being worked on (deleted or moved), the app starts no other job, not even the next entry of the queue; a request in that time is refused with a note. If the app restarts in that time (for example through a new ELF), the choice is gone: at the next start the history and a notification say what was open – if something had been deleted already, the notification says where the rest lies. If ShadowMountPlus ended an unpack without a result value, the image stays at “Delete” (at “Move” it goes on: the copy is always checked). The page sends the path of the original it showed; if the title lies somewhere else when the job starts, the app refuses. A folder with an unfinished rest of an earlier copy of this app at the target does not count as taken: the copy replaces it. If the target folder is on the same drive as the original (not on the internal SSD, whose game folders are mounts of their own), the original is only renamed: at once, without a copy and without free room; if that is not possible between the two places, it is copied after all.

PS4 game folders (only sce_sys/param.sfo, no param.json) can be converted too since version 1.75.0: ShadowMountPlus mounts PS4 images from 1.7beta8 on, in all three formats. The app puts a param.json built from the param.sfo into the image, so older versions find it as well. The target can only be a USB or M.2 drive – a PS4 title from the console's storage crashes it. Trophies do not work for PS4 games from images (0x80551618), and some titles get stuck at “Please wait”: both need a real installation (“Packages” tab).

Unsigned executables: If a game's executables (eboot.bin, .prx, .sprx, .elf, .self) are plain ELF files, the console does not start it: its loader refuses such files. The convert window names them beforehand (“Unsigned executables”). The image gets them fake-signed as FSELF, in the layout that make_fself.py of ampr-emu-ng and ps5-dump-forge write; the game folder is only read. An ampr_emu.index in the folder is brought to the new sizes at the same time. Executables that are already signed stay as they are; ones with an unusual structure the app leaves unchanged and says so.

Check before the start, name, steps and queue (since 13.11.2026). The conversion window checks everything at once before the start and shows it as a list: source readable, space on the target, FAT32 (no file over 4 GB), a name that already exists at the target, a running game. Red blocks the start, yellow only warns. Since 22.11.2026 the list also names a damaged home-screen picture (icon0, pic0, pic1 or pic2.png in sce_sys, not a valid PNG), in yellow: the app takes it over unchanged, and it may be missing on the home screen. The name of the result follows the game's folder; with a template made of {titel}, {id}, {version} and {quelle} you can change it, for example {titel} [{id}] v{version}, and the window shows the finished name and its length. While it runs, one line shows the steps (measuring, writing, with ffpfsc compressing, checking, renaming) with the time each one took. With Add to queue you line up several games one after the other: if something else is already running, the entry waits and starts by itself afterwards; an error does not stop the queue, and a failed entry can be tried again. The queue lives in the app's memory and is empty after a restart. If the source changes (a file replaced, deleted or new) while the app converts, it does not adopt the result and names the file.

Debug FPKG (since 1.84.0). Besides ffpfsc, ffpkg and exFAT the window builds a debug FPKG (.pkg) that Kraken Mount mounts (tab “FPKGMount”). It is written by Dump Forge (quer3q, GPL-3.0), a PS5 program of its own: the app starts it for the job, gives it the source and the target, shows its steps (Measure, Compress, Check, Rename) as with the other formats and stops it again afterwards; “Add to queue” works too. Dump Forge is part of the app: its ELF (17.7 MiB) lies packed (zstd, 8.0 MiB) in the app’s ELF and so in both tiles, so whoever only uses the ELF has nothing to fetch. A newer version takes precedence over the built-in one (0.5.7): “Download newer version from GitHub” in the window fetches it (only on a button press, HTTPS, the checksum from SHA256SUMS is compared), or you put ps5-dump-forge-<version>-ps5.elf (the version only digits and dots, newer than 0.5.7) into the folder /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/dumpforge/ yourself (for example by FTP); the newest version counts. There are four compression levels: Fast (Kraken, recommended), Balanced and Smallest (about 2.6% smaller, but about 6 and 9 times as long, with every core busy throughout) and Uncompressed (the package as big as the game, for the case that the console does not start a compressed one). “Playable” puts the package into the FPKG-Games folder of the target, which Kraken Mount searches; “Backup” puts it into PS5-Sicherung/Spiele. The name of the result may have at most 63 bytes (without “.pkg”); the window checks this before the start. With Thorough Dump Forge reads every byte of the finished package again; with Quick it checks the structure, small files in full and a sample of the rest; no checksum file is created. If the original has the same title ID and is mounted by ShadowMountPlus, the two get in each other’s way as soon as Kraken Mount registers the package: unmount the original first. Dump Forge makes no tile on the home screen: the app keeps the place /user/app/PDFG00001 occupied with an empty file (as with Kraken Mount) and removes a tile made earlier at the next start. Games with AMPR packs (since 18 November 2026): if the game is packed with AMPR packs (ampr_zstd.index or ampr_assets.index in the folder or the image), Dump Forge unpacks the packs itself while converting (zstd packs with “zstd_unpack”, LZ4 packs with “lz4: unpack” in its job), because Kraken Mount does not accept a package with packs in it and it would show as “Failed” in its list. The package then holds the unpacked game and gets as big as that (smaller, depending on the level), the source stays unchanged, and it takes longer than for a game without packs. The window says so beforehand: for a folder it names the size of the unpacked game (from the packs’ index) and checks the room against it, for an image only Dump Forge can say how big it gets; the check before the start shows a yellow note. “FPKG” stays greyed out only when it cannot be checked whether the game holds packs, or when it has zstd and LZ4 packs together (Dump Forge unpacks one kind only): then first unpack one kind (“Unpack zstd” or “Unpack LZ4” under the game’s asset packs), then convert.

Packing while converting (since 19.11.2026). For exFAT and ffpkg of a PS5 game folder, the convert window shows a group Packing (AMPR packs): Do not pack (the default; the app writes the image itself as before), LZ4 packs or zstd packs (AMPR EMU NG only). You also choose the level (LZ4: 9 balanced, recommended, 3 fast, 12 smallest; zstd: 5 balanced, recommended, 1 fastest, 9 smaller, 19 smallest) and, for LZ4, the runtime in the game: AMPR EMU NG (the default) or original APR-EMU (only for games that load libSceAmpr themselves; Dump Forge refuses it otherwise). The image is then written by Dump Forge (version 0.5.6 or newer; the app carries 0.5.7), which packs the game on the fly: the files go into the packs while the image is written, with no temporary folder and without first making a packed copy of the game. The original stays unchanged. The steps: Measure (the files to pack are computed once and nothing is written; the window says “The game is being measured for the packs …” and then shows a percentage and the time left, an estimate), Write (“is being packed and written”, with a percentage and the time left instead of sizes) and Check. Dump Forge reads the source twice for this, so it takes longer than without packing. At the end the window says “<size> instead of <size of the game> (n %)”.

Dump Forge decides which files are packed: with AMPR EMU NG (zstd, and LZ4 with the NG runtime) everything except the system files (programs, sce_sys, sce_module, fakelib, empty files); with the original APR-EMU a more careful LZ4 method that leaves media, configuration files and the files in the root folder loose. There is no profile as with “Pack in the game folder”. For zstd (for any game) and for LZ4 with the NG runtime, Dump Forge puts AMPR EMU NG itself into the game as fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx (in Dump Forge 0.5.7: v0.4.1); with the original APR-EMU the APR-EMU built into Dump Forge goes in. Another NG version can be installed afterwards under “APR-EMU in the game”. “Build the AMPR index first” does not apply (Dump Forge writes the index itself). The check afterwards (Thorough or Quick) stays and is done by Dump Forge; no checksum file (.sha256) is made. The name of the result may be at most 63 bytes long (without “.exfat” or “.ffpkg”), as for the FPKG; on a FAT32 drive the limit of 4 GB is only a warning here, because the image gets smaller than the game (by how much, only Dump Forge knows). The choice is greyed out (with the reason in the window) for PS4 games (they have no AMPR packs), for a game that already lies in LZ4 or zstd packs (unpack it first with the game’s asset packs, then convert), and when it cannot be checked whether it holds packs. For ffpfsc there is no such choice: its compression is already in the image. “Add to queue” and “Original afterwards” work as for the other formats; the queue names the entry with “LZ4 packs” or “zstd packs”, the history with “exfat + LZ4”. Try it on a small game first: whether a packed game runs depends, as always, on AMPR EMU NG (or the APR-EMU), and the original stays unchanged anyway.

Dump Forge with the plain ELF

If you only use the ELF (no tile), you no longer have to fetch Dump Forge: the app carries Dump Forge 0.5.7 packed (since 21 Nov 2026; the ELF is about 8 MiB bigger for it), unpacks it in memory for every job, checks its size and checksum and sends it to the payload loader; nothing is written to the console for it. A newer version comes in two ways:

  1. Let the app load it: In the convert window choose the format “FPKG (debug .pkg)” and press Download newer version from GitHub. If there is a newer version, the app fetches it (about 18 MB) from GitHub, compares the checksum from SHA256SUMS and saves it; otherwise it reports that the newest one is already there.
  2. Put it there by hand: copy the file ps5-dump-forge-VERSION-ps5.elf (the version only digits and dots and newer than the built-in 0.5.7, for example 0.5.8; a file with no version in its name such as ps5-dump-forge.elf, or an older version, the app passes over) by FTP (port 2121) or with the file manager to /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/dumpforge/. The app makes the folder at every start. The file must be 1 to 40 MiB, an ELF file and whole (for the built-in version the app checks the SHA-256 checksum, for a newer one that the file is not cut off; a file that fails is passed over and the built-in version is used); the app does not need a restart.

If several versions are there, the app takes the highest; with the same version a file in the app's folder wins over the built-in one and over the folders of the tiles, and a file with no version in its name (ps5-dump-forge.elf) is older than the built-in one. The app starts and ends Dump Forge by itself for every job.

{{FIG:04-spiele-konvertieren.png}}
Please recreate .ffpkg images made with versions before 1.48.0 (old structure).

PS4 games from USB (PS4Mount)

The tab PS4 PKG from USB on the games page plays PS4 games (fake PKG) straight from the USB drive without installing them. It is based on PS4Mount by gasb07 (GPL-3.0), whose source code has been taken into the app.

  1. Prepare. On an exFAT drive, put the game, its update and add-ons as .pkg anywhere on the drive, in any folders and with any file names (the settings can limit the search to certain folders). They belong together when they have the same title ID. The packages stay where they are; the app does not move anything (since PS4Mount 0.8.0).
  2. Switch on. The switch “Switch on” starts the search; it stays on across a restart of the app. “Search now” starts a search at once. Since 21 November 2026 PS4Mount is off by default (from 17 to 21 November 2026 it was on); if you switch it on, it stays on, and if you switch it off, it stays off: the app saves both.
  3. Wait. The app reads the drive once into an index (each PKG only once) and reports each game as soon as it is ready to play. The game appears on the home screen with its icon. When a game has several updates, the newest is used (“Updates” lets you choose another); when the same game is on two drives, the drive that added it first keeps it.
  • The PKG files stay on the drive; only small management files go to the console. Deleting a game on the console or with “Remove tile” only removes the tile from the home screen; the PKG stays on the USB drive, and “Restore tile” brings the tile back.
  • Found, not set up (since 29 Oct 2026): below the games, the tab lists the PKGs the search leaves alone, each with the reason: already installed on the console (delete the installed game first to play it from USB), not fully copied yet (the file is smaller than its header says), not a PS4 package (for example a PS5 PKG, which the “Packages” tab installs), not a fake PKG, an add-on without a PS4 game or with add-ons switched off, a second copy of a file already in use, a damaged game package (since PS4Mount 0.7.1: malformed IDs in its param.sfo; such a package can power the console off and damage its storage, so it is never registered), on the M.2 expansion (since 23 Nov 2026: the console does not start PS4 games from there, tried on the Slim with error 0x80B2150F; put the PKGs on a USB stick with exFAT, add-ons included). The list is also shown in the full-screen app.
  • Updates (patch.pkg) and add-ons (DLC) are included; add-ons only when the switch in the settings is on.
  • Drive under another name (since PS4Mount 0.6.1): if the same drive comes back as usb1 instead of usb0 after a restart, the games stay registered; the app only rewrites the links to the new folder.
  • No merged PKGs: game PKGs with patches, add-ons or updates already merged into them may not work. Better use the original game PKG and put the update and add-ons beside it as separate .pkg files. A game PKG is only used from the folder of its own title ID.
  • The app has to be running for the games to stay visible after a console restart. If PS4Mount already runs as a payload of its own (ps4mount.elf), the app does not load its PS4Mount a second time: the tab shows “waiting”, and once the stand-alone one has ended, the app takes over by itself. It is recognised by its web panel (port 8770), the lock on port 9032 or its process name; if it turns up later, for example after rest mode, the app stops its own. The other way round, the Payloads page (a startup profile too) does not start a ps4mount.elf while a PS4Mount is already running.
  • Firmware (since PS4Mount 0.4.4): from 6.00 the console registers the games the usual way (tested on 13.20, reported on 6.50); below 6.00 one at a time, and where that function is missing no games are added, to protect the database. The notification at switch-on names the way. This version inside the app has been checked on a PS5 Pro with 12.00: PS4 games from a USB drive are added and run. It is switched off until you switch it on.

Move PKGs back (since PS4Mount 0.5.0; since 0.8.0 the game stays in the library): Earlier versions of PS4Mount moved the PKGs to ps4/CUSAxxxxx and recorded in ps4/CUSAxxxxx/origin.txt where every PKG came from. “Move PKGs back” on a game (only for games with PKGs in ps4/CUSAxxxxx), “Move selected back” or “Move all back” puts the game, update, older updates and add-ons back in their old place with their original names. The game stays in the library and keeps being played from there; if you no longer want to play it from USB, take its tile out with “Remove tile”. A running game is closed first, even a PS5 game. A missing folder is created; an existing file is never replaced (then “ (1)” is added to the name). PKGs that older versions moved end up at the top level as CUSAxxxxx - Name - game.pkg. No PKG is deleted.

  • Close PS4Mount games before rest mode. Rest mode switches the drive off; a game left open cannot read afterwards and locks up.
  • Switching off unmounts the games (since PS4Mount 0.7.2): switching PS4Mount off before rest mode is safe. The app unmounts every game, without forcing; while a game is open it refuses and names it. If a game folder is still in use, it mounts all of them again and asks you to try again in a moment. Switched on, PS4Mount mounts the games again.
  • Two or more connected drives (partitions count too) can make the console interface slow, with or without PS4Mount. Then connect a single drive with one partition.
  • A running game can use at most about 30 packages (game, update and roughly 29 add-ons with data; unlock-only add-ons no longer count since PS4Mount 0.7.3). This is a console limit that applies to installed games too.
  • Since 0.7.3 PS4Mount handles up to 768 games per drive (before: 256) and searches up to 64 folders (before: 8). Anything beyond that is reported instead of being skipped silently.

Before packing to ffpfsc: the console has to unpack a compressed file over and over while playing, so games with a great deal of data or texture streaming can stutter. Before the app converts a game (dump folder, .exfat, .ffpkg or .ffpfs) to .ffpfsc it looks: from about 40 GB of data, with large streaming containers (.ucas, .utoc, .pak, .forge, .streamdb, .resources, .cas, .rpf; 4 GB together or more) or with a streaming folder (2 GB or more) the window shows a note next to “ffpfsc”. There is no second question: “Start” converts. This is an estimate from file names and sizes, not from the game engine.

(F)PKG games with Kraken Mount (FPKGMount)

The FPKGMount tab next to “PS4 PKG from USB” plays (F)PKG games and game folders (plain, zstd, LZ4) straight from the disk or a USB drive without installing them. For this the app brings the program Kraken Mount by quer3q (GPL-3.0, version 0.3.1; a program of its own, not rewritten into the app), starts it and shows its games.

Kraken Mount from version 0.2.0: The program itself waits after its start until ShadowMountPlus has ended and registers no game until then. So that FPKGMount works next to ShadowMountPlus as before, the app changes only the name of the process it waits for in the built-in version (and in one loaded from GitHub) (shadowmountplus.elf, one byte): it then finds none and does not wait. The wait for kstuff stays. A Kraken Mount ELF that you send to the ELF loader yourself keeps waiting for ShadowMountPlus; the page then shows “waiting for ShadowMountPlus”.
  • Preparing: An unencrypted debug FPKG (for example from Dump Forge) as a .pkg goes into the folder FPKG-Games: on the internal storage /data/FPKG-Games (the app creates it at the first start), on a USB or M.2 drive the folder FPKG-Games in the main folder (you create that one yourself). Kraken Mount searches only these folders, and ShadowMountPlus does not search there: so the two do not get in each other’s way, and your game folders and images stay with ShadowMountPlus. The search folders are in the configuration of Kraken Mount, which the app creates at the first start when there is none; an existing one stays as it is (the page names the folders that apply; they can be changed on the page of Kraken Mount itself, port 8097). Backports go to <search folder>/backports/<TITLE-ID>*.
  • Switching on: “Switch on” sends the program to the ELF loader. Every game gets a notification and a tile of its own. The app does not create a tile for Kraken Mount itself (there is only the page in the app, as with “PS4 PKG from USB”); a tile Kraken Mount made earlier is removed at the next start. The same switch stops it; stopping is refused while a game runs. Since 21 Nov 2026 Kraken Mount is off by default (from 17 to 21 Nov 2026 the app started it by itself). If you switch it on, the app starts it by itself every time it starts (after about 5 seconds); the app remembers switching it on as it remembers switching it off (file kraken/zustand.txt in the app's data folder). If an older version of Kraken Mount still runs after an update of the app (it keeps running independently of the app), the page says so: switching it off and on again starts the new one.
  • List: name, title ID, version, size, drive, kind (FPKG or folder) and state. Rebuild builds a game's cache again (it always lives on the internal SSD under /data/krakenmount/caches). Delete game asks first and deletes the PKG file or game folder, the tile and the cache; saves stay. Turn PlayGo stub off or on (from Kraken Mount 0.3.1; only for games that load PlayGo) switches the bundled PlayGo stub off for this game alone when the game stays on a black screen with it (Resident Evil Village and some others); turn it on again when the game asks you to finish the download. Kraken Mount keeps the choice in its setting playgo_off.
  • Newer version: “Download newer version from GitHub” fetches the newest release (only when you press it, over HTTPS, with the checksum from SHA256SUMS); the next start uses it. The settings of Kraken Mount (search folders, fakelib) stay on its own page (port 8097, link in the tab).
  • New in version 0.3.0 (18 Nov 2026): saves no longer use the libSceSaveData.native.sprx from a game's fakelib (it made saves disappear); .pkg games always get ampr-emu-ng; the bundled emulators for DLC (dlc_emu 0.3) and PlayGo (pgo_stub 0.6) go into the fakelib of a game that needs them and does not bring a newer copy; a game that is still being copied is skipped until its files have not changed for 10 seconds. When a game's source is missing for 5 minutes (for example an unplugged drive), Kraken Mount removes it from the home screen; the cache stays, and the game returns with its source. On Kraken Mount's own page (port 8097) every USB drive has an eject button, and the new settings are there too (add_emulators, stability_wait_seconds, auto_remove_missing). At the first start after the change Kraken Mount puts every game's fakelib together once more; that takes a while.
  • New in version 0.3.1 (20 Nov 2026): On firmware 12 and newer games register on the home screen again: where the call for a single game is missing, each search pass prepares its games and registers them at the end with one call (one message for the whole group). New is the PlayGo stub switch for each game (see above). Games in a folder directly inside a search folder are found too; registering a game is faster (about 21 instead of 36 to 44 seconds); every line in kraken.log starts with the time; a wrong item in a list of the settings is skipped and the others stay. AMPR EMU NG 0.5.0 is bundled.
  • Notes: Kraken Mount is a beta; as a .pkg a game may run worse than as a zstd folder. If you point Kraken Mount at folders that ShadowMountPlus searches too (for example /data/homebrew), every game folder there would be registered twice. After a restart of the console Kraken Mount must be running for the games to stay visible. The full-screen app has the same page under Games → FPKGMount (square: rebuild, delete; triangle: start/stop, search, newer version, log). A game whose param.json has “upgradable” as applicationDrmType (many images do) gets a padlock on its tile, because Kraken Mount registers the file unchanged; ShadowMountPlus rewrites it to “standard” while registering. The game still starts.

The card of a game that Kraken Mount mounted carries the mark FPKGMount (like PS4Mount for the PS4 games from USB): it was not installed by a package installer but runs from the debug package.

chapters.title: AMPR index, APR-EMU, PlayGo and history
chapters.html:
Every game card has the button LZ4/zstd asset packs … under Convert. It opens a window with tools around APR-EMU. It holds the AMPR index, APR-EMU in the game and PlayGo in the game, packing into LZ4 or zstd packs, the Optimization by recording, the Game plugins and, for an image, checking, unpacking and repairing. For an image the button is called AMPR & APR-EMU …: LZ4 and zstd work only with dump folders.

  • The AMPR index (ampr_emu.index) is the list of all of the game's files that APR-EMU needs to find them. The window shows whether there is one and how many files it knows.
  • Build / Rebuild creates it. For a dump folder this happens directly; for an image, ShadowMountPlus briefly mounts it for writing and unmounts it afterwards. An old index stays as ampr_emu.index.bak.
  • When converting a dump folder there is the box Build the AMPR index first (already ticked for games with APR-EMU; it is missing for PS4 games, for the format FPKG and when packing while converting). This puts the index inside the image – for a compressed image (.ffpfsc) it is the only way, as nothing can be written there afterwards.
A running game and any other job of the app block building. The layout follows drakmor's script build_ampr_index.py (GPL-3.0) and was compared byte for byte with its result.

APR-EMU in the game

The row APR-EMU in the game shows which libSceAmpr.sprx a game loads and lets you choose a version and put it in, bring the game's original back or remove the file. The versions are files in /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/AMPR_EMU, named like drakmor's releases (libSceAmpr.sprx-0.4.2.1-test-pack). Seven versions are bundled with the app: they show in the list even when they are not in the folder yet, and get there when you build one in or with Put the bundled versions into the folder (the folder is made when needed). Add more with Add file. Every file is checked (SELF header, the mark “[AMPR_EMU]”). Variants with “pack” in the name can read LZ4 packs, “debug” writes a log.

The list of versions has three groups, each with its own title: AMPR EMU NG @quer3q (all NG versions, including those added later), AMPR EMU @Drakmor (the version without pack support, listed as just 0.4.2.1) and LZ4 asset pack version (the two versions that serve LZ4 packs only, test-pack and test-debug-pack).

AMPR EMU NG (quer3q, ampr-emu-ng, GPL-3.0) is a further development of ampr_emu and reads LZ4 and zstd packs. Its files carry the mark “ampr-emu-ng <version>”; in the list they appear at the top with the tag NG (NG 0.5.0, NG 0.5.0 debug, NG 0.4.1, NG 0.4.1 debug). Two versions are offered; the app carries libSceAmpr.sprx-0.5.0-ng, -ng-debug, libSceAmpr.sprx-0.4.1-ng, -ng-debug. The button Check for a new AMPR EMU NG version and load it asks GitHub for the newest stable release (the app never takes a beta); if it is newer than all offered, the app loads its two files into the AMPR_EMU folder, checks them against the SHA256SUMS of the release and the mark, puts it at the top of the list and lets the oldest version drop out (the files of it that the app stored are deleted, your own files stay). Loading happens only when you press the button. Add file renames files of a newer release (libSceAmpr.sprx, libSceAmpr-debug.sprx) to fit. When installing NG, the app asks whether to turn off the automatic fakelib update in ShadowMountPlus, because otherwise ShadowMountPlus replaces the NG file again at the start of a game with the version from its emulator folder: Yes sets only the line update_emulators in /data/shadowmount/config.ini to 0 (the app saves the file once as config.ini.ps5cc-bak) and installs NG, Cancel leaves everything as it is. Depending on its version, ShadowMountPlus takes the change over at once or at its next start. From 1.7beta12 ShadowMountPlus uses a new format for config.ini (sections; the setting is called update_enabled under [emulators]) and converts the old files at its first start (the old ones stay in config-v1-backup); the app understands both formats and leaves comments and everything else in the file as it is. The app finds out which version you run from the file (default: Detect automatically); you can set it with From 1.7beta12 or Before 1.7beta12 in the browser on the System page, at the very top in the ShadowMountPlus card, in the fullscreen app under System → ShadowMountPlus. Which line is written is decided by the file itself as soon as it shows its format; your answer applies to a missing or empty config.ini and triggers a hint when it does not fit the file (for example when ShadowMountPlus has not been started since the update and the file is still the old one). The question does not appear when the update is already off. The same setting is also available as the switch Update fakelib automatically in the ShadowMountPlus card on the System page (full-screen app: System → ShadowMountPlus); there you can turn it on or off by hand at any time.

  • Where the file goes follows ShadowMountPlus (1.7beta1 and newer): it looks first in the backport folder <scan path>/backports/<title id>/ (since 1.7beta6 also a folder whose name only begins with the title id, such as “PPSA12345 Game Name”: the one named exactly like it wins, otherwise the first in byte order), then in the game, and the first folder that exists counts alone. For a game folder, .exfat or .ffpkg it goes to fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx in the game (an image is briefly mounted for writing by ShadowMountPlus). A compressed .ffpfsc cannot be written: a backport folder is made there and the game stays untouched; because it hides the game's fakelib, its files are copied in. If a backport folder already exists, it is used for every format. For an image (.exfat, .ffpkg) you can also choose the backport folder under “Where does the file go?”; if the image is full (“No space left on device”), the app puts the file there by itself.
  • The file the game brought itself is kept once as libSceAmpr.sprx.orig and never overwritten; an earlier APR-EMU does not count as an original. Restore original puts it back. Remove deletes only the APR-EMU file.
  • The window warns when a fakelib2 lies beside fakelib (ShadowMountPlus from 1.7beta1 then reads only that one), and when ShadowMountPlus replaces the file at the start of a game from /data/shadowmount/emus (update_emulators=1, from 1.7beta12 update_enabled under [emulators]). A game in LZ4 packs accepts only versions with “pack” and cannot otherwise be changed.

LZ4 asset packs (short version)

The step-by-step guide with troubleshooting is in the chapter LZ4 asset packs: step by step. Only a game that links libSceAmpr can be packed; otherwise the button is locked.

The row LZ4 asset packs packs the data of a game into seekable LZ4 packs (ampr_assets-NNN.pak, directory ampr_assets.index) that APR-EMU reads while you play and unpacks block by block. The game then takes up less space. It only works for games that are a folder (turn an image into a folder first with Unpack into a folder) and only for games that use APR-EMU: the app puts the APR-EMU version “0.4.2.1 test-pack” into fakelib (the game's own file is kept as .orig), because only the “pack” versions read packs.

The settings window (Pack with LZ4 …) asks three things:

  • How strongly? Level 3 (LZ4 Fast, quick), 9 (LZ4 HC, balanced) or 12 (LZ4 HC, smallest).
  • What goes in? If a bundled tested profile fits the game, it is at the top and already selected (see the chapter “LZ4 asset packs: step by step”). Automatic: game data is packed; programs (eboot.bin, .sprx/.prx), sce_sys, fakelib, saved data and media that is already compressed (mp4, ogg, wem …) stay loose, and so do very large files that hardly compress. Or an own profile (TOML) in the format of drakmor's ampr_pack.py ([pack], [groups.NAME], [[rule]] with include/exclude, block_size, layout, compress/store/loose, [runtime]; lists for include_from lie beside it). Profiles live in the folder /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/LZ4_Profile or in the folder LZ4_Profile of a USB drive; Add profile … uploads a file there. Programs, system folders and the packs themselves always stay loose, even with a profile. Before the start the window shows how many files will be packed.
  • What happens to the originals? Pack in the game folder: the AMPR index is built afresh, the files are packed, every file is compared byte for byte with its original and only then is the original removed; on any error the packs are removed again and everything stays as before. Or as a new folder <name>-lz4 beside the game: the original stays untouched, the loose files are copied and read back.

A packed game carries the tag LZ4 packed on its card (zstd packed for zstd packs; it appears for every format, also for an image). The row then offers Check packs (every block is read, unpacked and checked against its checksum) and Unpack LZ4 … (writes the files back, compares them with the packs and then removes the packs). While a game is packed, the AMPR index is locked and the APR-EMU can only be swapped for another “pack” version: the packs belong to exactly this index.

The app keeps packing at low priority even if the window is closed; a running game must be closed first. Format (AMPRPAK4/AMPRDAT3) and rules follow drakmor's ampr_emu (GPL-3.0); packing and checking are tested against its Python tool in both directions. Files a game reads through mmap do not belong in packs – the automatic selection therefore leaves programs and system files out.

PlayGo in the game

The row PlayGo in the game works the same way for libScePlayGo.sprx, drakmor's PlayGo stub (pgo_stub, GPL-3.0): it reports everything as completely installed to a game whose PlayGo content cannot be found (any more). It only helps with games that treat PlayGo content as missing. The versions are files in the folder /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/PlayGo (libScePlayGo.sprx-0.6-nolog, libScePlayGo.sprx-0.6-log); both 0.6 builds come with the app, and “log” writes /app0/playlgo.log into the game. Each file is checked (SELF header, mark “playgo_stub.dat”). Place, the backup as libScePlayGo.sprx.orig, the backport folder for a .ffpfsc, the warnings and removing work as with the APR-EMU file; LZ4 packs play no part for PlayGo. The two files of a game can be changed independently of each other. A stub in the emulator folder of ShadowMountPlus (/data/shadowmount/emus/libScePlayGo.sprx) wins here too.

Check, unpack, repair an image

If the game is an image (.exfat, .ffpkg or .ffpfsc), the same window has three more tools. The app reads the image itself, without mounting it; a running game and any other job of the app block them.

  • Check image: for an .ffpfsc the whole container is read first (header, block table, every block unpacked – every block carries a checksum), then the files in it are checked to lie where the file system says. For .exfat and .ffpkg every file is read in full (a drive that is going bad shows there). If the check finds something, the window names the affected files, with the place where it starts. The result stays in the window until the app restarts.
  • Unpack into a folder: writes all files to homebrew/<name of the image> on a drive of your choice. Beforehand the window shows files, size, room and file system of every drive (FAT32 takes no files over 4 GB). Each file is written into a folder ending in .ps5cc-teil, read back from the drive and compared with what came from the image (CRC-32). Only when everything matches does the folder get its name; on an error or a cancel it is removed again. The image stays untouched; the game then exists twice.
  • Repair: only where it is safe. If the size of an .ffpfsc file does not match the image's header, but the data is complete and the extra bytes are empty, the app sets the size right and reads the container in full once more. Damaged blocks cannot be made again from the image alone. Repair is locked while ShadowMountPlus has the image mounted.

History

On the games page the History tab lists all of the app's jobs – copy, convert, split package, install, delete, file manager, saved data, disc images, dumps, AMPR index, APR-EMU and PlayGo, LZ4 packs, and checking, unpacking and repairing an image – with result (done, failed, cancelled), size, duration and time. The last 500 are kept on the console in /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/history.jsonl. Clear history deletes them after a question.

Game plugins

The row Game plugins keeps drakmor's replacement modules in the game's fakelib folder up to date: the PlayGo stub (libScePlayGo.sprx, pgo_stub 0.6) and the DLC modules (libSceAppContent.sprx, libSceGameUpdate.sprx, libSceNpEntitlementAccess.sprx, dlc_emu 0.3, “log” build: it writes /app0/dlc_emu.log into the game; the build without logging crashed at game start and is replaced as a “faulty build”) that show the DLC listed in the game's dlc_emu.ini as owned.

  • An older build (the app knows it by its checksum) is replaced, the old file stays as .old. A file of an unknown build is left alone.
  • The PlayGo stub is never added to a game that has none; that is done in the row “PlayGo in the game”. The DLC modules are only added when the game folder holds a dlc_emu.ini (without it they would hide the real DLC).
  • If a library lacks the execute permission (the app created them like that until 13 Oct 2026), “Update” sets it. Without it the console does not load it (“mount flag / attribute error”).
  • If the game has a fakelib2 or ShadowMountPlus reads a backport folder, the app changes nothing.

chapters.title: LZ4 asset packs: step by step
chapters.html:
An asset pack is a few files (ampr_assets-000.pak and more, plus ampr_assets.index). The app packs a game's data into them and shrinks it with LZ4. APR-EMU reads them while you play and unpacks each block only when the game needs it. According to the developer (drakmor, ampr_emu) this halves the space and often loads 30 to 40 percent faster. Version 0.4.2.1 is expressly a test version: not every game tolerates it.

What you need

  • The game is a folder. Turn an image into a folder first with Unpack to a folder.
  • The game links libSceAmpr. The app looks for the name in eboot.bin and in sce_module and shows ✓ loads libSceAmpr itself. If it says ✗ does not load libSceAmpr itself, the button is locked: the game would not find its files in the packs. Such games can only be compressed to an .ffpfsc image (button Convert).
  • A current ShadowMountPlus, with images mounted read-only (the default).
  • Space: when packing inside the game folder the app needs about half of the game data extra until the originals are removed.

Step by step

  1. Install APR-EMU. In the window LZ4/zstd asset packs & APR-EMU, under APR-EMU in the game, choose version 0.4.2.1 test-pack. Only versions with “pack” in the name read packs.
  2. Test unpacked. Start the game and play for a while: menu, a level, load a save. If it does not run like this, it will never run packed. Then only an older APR-EMU (for example 0.3.6.6; it has not come with the app since November 2026, Add file takes it from drakmor's releases page) or none helps.
  3. Pack. Pack with LZ4 …, to begin with level 9 and Automatic. The box “started unpacked, and it ran” belongs to it. Pack in the game folder saves the most space; the originals are removed only once every file has been compared byte for byte with the packs, and on any error everything stays as before. The choice As a new folder … next to it leaves the original untouched but puts two folders with the same title ID side by side. ShadowMountPlus can choke on that and keep re-mounting the game every few seconds; take the original out of the search path first. If there is a tested profile for the game (see below), it is already selected.
  4. Check packs. Reads every block, decompresses it and compares it with the CRC file. Then it fixes what good packs also need: if the APR-EMU that reads packs is missing or something replaced it, 0.4.2.1 test-pack goes back in. Files the PS5 looks for on the drive but that only exist inside the packs (packed by older tools) are brought back. And it sets the permissions in the game folder to 0777. What it fixed is listed under Repaired. No repacking is needed. This shows that the packs are intact, not that the game uses them correctly.
  5. Start and play. Only now you see whether it runs. Play for longer than a few seconds: menu, a level, loading and saving.
  6. If it does not run: Unpack LZ4 … writes all files back, compares them and removes the packs.

Tested profiles

The app ships four profiles that danthespal wrote and tested on the console (published with MkPFS.CSharp, also shipped by LZ4 Compression): ASTRO BOT, EA Sports UFC 6, the Insomniac engine (tested with Marvel's Wolverine) and the Unity engine (tested with God of War Sons of Sparta). If one fits the game, by title ID, name or file layout, the row shows ✓ tested profile, and it is already selected when you pack. A profile of your own for the game (file name starting with the title ID, for example from the recording) comes first. Under Own profile the four can also be chosen for other games. Each leaves files it does not name loose: another version of the game packs less with it but stays safe.

What always stays loose

Whatever the profile: empty files, the PlayGo markers (cache_ps5/pgc_*_dummy_file, cache_ps5/playgo.pgm) and the boot files Ghost of Yōtei needs to get past the black screen, as well as the pack tables *.rmdtoc (Alan Wake 2), stay loose. The PS5 looks for them on the drive outside the game, where the APR-EMU cannot help (found for LZ4 Compression 1.4.3). Everything the app writes into a game folder gets the permissions 0777, also when copying, when unpacking an image and in the file manager.

What “Automatic” leaves loose

With the profile Automatic, these stay loose: programs and libraries (eboot.bin, .prx, .sprx), sce_sys, sce_module, fakelib, saves, already compressed media (mp4, webm, ogg, wem …), configuration and data files (.json, .xml, .ini, .dat, .bin, .utoc), archives (.zip, .7z, .rar) and the game's own .pak files, the folders trophy2, uds, _DUPLEX_, decrypted and movie folders, Wwise sound banks (soundbank…, wem…), files directly in the game folder and very large files that hardly pack. This is the list that has proved itself in tools that run on the console (exFAT2AMPR by V-10, Lazy_AMPR). A profile of your own (TOML) packs what its rules say.

If the game does not start or crashes

  • First find out who is to blame. Unpack the game and start it unpacked with the same APR-EMU version. Example Arkanoid (12 Oct 2026): with 0.4.2.1 it crashed even unpacked, with 0.3.6.6 it ran. Packs were not possible there.
  • “mount flag / attribute error” in the ShadowMountPlus log: the library cannot be loaded because it lacks the execute permission (mode 0644). The app creates it with 0755. If you copied the file yourself, run SITE CHMOD 755 over FTP.
  • SIGBUS or CE-108255-1 right at the start: eboot.bin or modules lack the execute permission, typically after a copy from an .exfat image (files with 0666, seen with 007 First Light). Check packs sets the permissions in the whole game folder to 0777.
  • The window shows a notice under the packed game: eboot.bin must not be executed (“Check packs” sets the permissions), or ShadowMountPlus does not include a fakelib for the game (fakelib mode “Deactivated” for the game, or including is switched off in its settings). Then the APR-EMU that reads the packs is missing at the start and the game does not start; in the web interface of ShadowMountPlus set the game's mode to “Emulators” or “Full”.
  • It crashes after a few seconds although it ran unpacked: the game probably reads files the packs do not serve, above all through mmap (mapped into memory) or for writing. Such files must stay loose. Use your own profile (TOML, folder LZ4_Profile) and add a loose rule for the file at the end: the last matching rule wins. Which files the game could not open is written by the debug version (0.4.2.1 test-debug-pack) as apr.pack.open.fail in ampr_emu.log.
  • “Automatic” is only a start. It only knows what is on the disk. Profiles made from recordings of a real play session are more reliable (ampr_pack_profile.py from ampr_emu, MkPFS).

Better than “Automatic”: the recording

“Automatic” only knows what is on the disk. A profile made from a real play session is more reliable. The row Optimization by recording does that in four steps:

  1. Start recording. The app puts the debug APR-EMU (0.4.2.1 test-debug-pack) into a folder fakelib2 of the game and copies the other libraries over from fakelib (ShadowMountPlus then reads only fakelib2 and replaces nothing in it). Requirements: the game loads libSceAmpr, the AMPR index is built, it is not in packs.
  2. Play. Start the game, play for a while (menu, a level, loading a save) and quit it normally. The game writes ampr_commands.bin. The debug version is slower.
  3. Collect the session. The app copies the recording and its index to /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/traces/<title ID>/<n>/. The debug APR-EMU empties the recording at every launch, so collect after each session. Several sessions (other levels, other modes) make a better profile.
  4. Create the profile. All sessions become <title ID>-mitschnitt.toml in the folder LZ4_Profile. For every file read it fixes the block size (16 KiB to 1 MiB), the layout (random, mixed, streaming), “hot” and the treatment (media are stored, not packed) and sets the caches of the APR-EMU. Files the game never read stay loose. When packing, choose it under Own profile.

Then Stop recording: that removes fakelib2 again. A recording only shows what was read in the scenes you played; add rules of your own for the rest.

Limits and notes

  • Unsigned executables: when the app packs into a new folder next to the game, it writes plain ELF files as FSELF (see the chapter “Games”), because the console would not start them otherwise. Packing in the game folder leaves them as they are. Only with zstd, which always packs in the game folder, the switch “Sign executables as FSELF” (on by default) replaces them there with FSELF versions. The window shows beforehand how many there are.
  • APR-EMU rejects sets with more than 2,000,000 files, 16,000,000 blocks or 1,024 pack files. For big games the app uses larger blocks.
  • The index, .runtime and packs of a game belong together (same build ID). Never swap single parts and change nothing while the game runs.
  • According to its author APR-EMU 0.4.2.1 still has a crash with saves. Keep the original until you have played long enough.
  • While a game is packed, the AMPR index and the APR-EMU version are locked.
  • Models and rules: drakmor/ampr_emu (docs/ASSET_PACK_WORKFLOW_EN.md, GPL-3.0), theghostonline/PS5-LZ4-Compression and danthespal/MkPFS.CSharp. From LZ4 Compression 1.4.3 to 1.5.0 (Husam Osman, GPL-3.0) come the list of files that must stay loose, the permissions 0777, the repair during the check and the choice of tested profiles; rebuilt, not copied.
  • Ideas and knowledge: exFAT2AMPR by V-10 (GitHub, GPL-3.0 with additional terms, “Made by V-10”): the list that “Automatic” leaves loose, the recording for profile creation (its structure and constants follow his port of ampr_pack_profile.py) and the upkeep of the game plugins with their table of checksums.

zstd instead of LZ4 (for AMPR EMU NG)

Besides the LZ4 packs the app also makes zstd packs: Pack with zstd … (files ampr_zstd.index and ampr_zstd-000.pak and more). The format comes from quer3q (ampr-emu-ng); only AMPR EMU NG reads it, no other APR-EMU does. The app puts NG into fakelib itself while packing. If the automatic fakelib update of ShadowMountPlus is still on, the result shows a warning: turn it off (System page, ShadowMountPlus card, switch Update fakelib automatically; or install NG beforehand under APR-EMU in the game, which makes the app ask about it).

  • The whole game is packed except the system files: programs (eboot.bin, .sprx, .prx, .elf, .self), sce_sys, sce_module, fakelib, .ini files (such as dlc_emu.ini, which people edit by hand), empty files, the files of the packs and of the APR-EMU, and the few files the PS5 itself looks for on the drive. There is neither a profile nor “Automatic”: AMPR EMU NG serves a fully packed game.
  • Level 1 to 22 (the app offers 1, 5, 9 and 19; default 5). Higher levels save more space but pack much more slowly. While playing hardly anything changes: unpacking costs about the same little at every level. Every piece of 256 KiB is a zstd frame of its own with a checksum; what zstd cannot shrink stays raw.
  • Unlike LZ4, zstd gives no choice whether the originals stay: the app always packs in the game folder and removes the originals only after the byte-for-byte comparison (on an error everything stays as it was). Beforehand you confirm, as with LZ4, that the game ran unpacked with NG; the app builds NG in itself when it packs. Check packs and Unpack zstd … exist as with LZ4; unpacking brings all files back. Unsigned executables the app replaces in the game folder with FSELF versions when the switch “Sign executables as FSELF” is on (default; otherwise they stay).
  • A game lies in LZ4 packs or in zstd packs, never in both. To switch, unpack first. In a zstd game all versions except NG are locked in the window APR-EMU in the game.

Status: packing and checking are verified against the originals and against an independent reader of the format (the one in PS5 Dump & Image Converter); on the console, Matchbox Driving Adventures (6 GB, level 1, AMPR EMU NG 0.3.3) ran in the foreground for at least two minutes after packing with zstd and could then be unpacked completely (08.11.2026); whether another game runs packed depends on AMPR EMU NG. Try it first on a small game; if it does not run, “Unpack zstd …” brings all files back.

Packing while converting. A game folder can also be packed into LZ4 or zstd packs right when it is converted into an .exfat or .ffpkg image: Dump Forge writes the image and packs on the fly, without a packed folder being made first (chapter “Games”, section “Packing while converting”). There is no profile there and no choice of the APR-EMU version (with LZ4 only the Runtime in the game: AMPR EMU NG or APR-EMU original); a game that already lies in packs is not packed a second time, it has to be unpacked first.

Does the index fit into AMPR EMU NG?

AMPR EMU NG 0.4.0 builds tables from the pack index that must fit into its memory: at most 48 MiB, and of the whole index memory (64 MiB) the size of ampr_emu.index and 16 MiB of page cache are taken off first. If they do not fit, NG serves no packed file and the game does not start (at launch it shows “index tables need 49 MiB, over the 48 MiB beside the page cache; packed files not served”; this happened with Final Fantasy XVI and Demon's Souls, ampr-emu-ng #67, #61, #53). So for a game with a pack, the dialog “LZ4/zstd asset packs & APR-EMU” shows the line Does the index fit into AMPR EMU NG?: “fits”, “tight” (within 2 MiB of the limit) or “too big”, with the estimated tables in MiB; in the full-screen app it is under “INDEX TABLES (AMPR EMU NG)”. The app works it out from the header of ampr_zstd.index (zstd; NG takes it before the LZ4 pack) or ampr_assets.index (LZ4) and the size of ampr_emu.index; the formulas were checked with the maintainers of ampr-emu-ng. This describes NG 0.4.0, which the app no longer ships; the line in the app calculates by the model of NG 0.4.1 and 0.5.0 (see the next paragraph). It remains an estimate: a later version may move the limits, and NG's own message at launch is the binding one. According to the reports such a game starts with NG 0.3.4; otherwise it helps to pack the game with fewer files.
