From NG 0.4.1 (in the app both versions: 0.5.0 and 0.4.1) a different model applies than with 0.4.0: there is no 48 MiB limit and no paged reading any more; the view of all files of ampr_emu.index and the pack tables together must fit the index memory of 80 MiB. The row Does the index fit into AMPR EMU NG? calculates for this version; with 0.4.1 a game that was “too big” with 0.4.0 usually fits (Final Fantasy XVI, Demon's Souls). NG 0.5.0 has the same view and the same size of index memory; the app calculates alike for both versions it carries. This too is an estimate from the source of NG; the message NG gives at the start stays binding.

chapters.title: Deleting games & backups
chapters.html:
Every game card has Delete, and so does every entry in the Backups tab.

  • Installed games are uninstalled by the console itself – as with “Delete” in the menu, including updates and add-ons.
  • Games from ShadowMountPlus are unregistered first; then the image or the folder is deleted.
  • PS4 games from PS4Mount are taken out of the library by PS4Mount: it unmounts the game, then the console uninstalls it. The PKG files on the USB drive stay where they are; they can be deleted in the file manager.
  • The app's backups (copies and conversions) are deleted together with their checksum file.
  1. Tap Delete: the app asks the console what will go and shows it in a window. Only Delete in the window deletes; Cancel leaves everything as it was.
  2. A progress bar with a percentage shows how far it has got.
  3. If the console refuses (for example because the game is running), the window stays open with the reason and nothing is deleted.
Your saved data is always kept. A running game is never deleted.

Only what really lies inside the game folder or image is deleted: if the path is behind a link or is a mounted drive, the app deletes nothing and says so.

{{FIG:08-spiele-sicherungen.png}}

chapters.title: Play time
chapters.html:
When you played, for how long and how warm the console got: totals for today, 7 and 30 days, the last 14 days as bars, the most played games and the recent sessions with peak temperatures. Can be saved as a spreadsheet (CSV).

The app counts these times itself, from the first start with this version on; the play time on the cards in the library, by contrast, comes from the console. Time counts while a game is in front: if it is paused on the home screen, the clock stops. “Delete history” starts the count over after a question; the games and their saved data stay.

{{FIG:05-spiele-spielzeit.png}}

chapters.title: Back up saved data
chapters.html:
Copies the saved data as the console stores it – encrypted, without opening or changing anything – to a USB stick, a disk or the internal SSD (PS5-Sicherung/Spielstaende/<Datum>). Every file is verified; “Verify” reads a backup again later.

Restore works for individual games: the app first backs up the current state, writes all new files next to the old ones first, verifies them and only then replaces the old ones.

Backing up and restoring only happen when no game is running – not even a paused one. Backups from another console cannot be restored.

Per user, split into PS5 games and PS4 games. Apps such as YouTube are not listed: the app changes nothing there – it does not back up, restore or delete anything of theirs. “Delete” removes the saved games of one title after a question that names it; the app first backs up the current state to the chosen drive (otherwise the first suitable one) and lets you put it back. If there is no drive at all, a note says that it is deleted without a backup.

Transfer to another console. A backup belongs to its console and cannot be opened on another one. So every PS5 title has the button “As ZIP”: the console reads the saved data out in the clear with its own means (the app decrypts nothing itself), and the app packs the files together with chives.json – which says how the image was built – into a ZIP file. It waits for download in the section “Transfer to another console” (on the console in /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/savexport); “Delete” removes it again. The file is not encrypted: only pass it on if you want to. Saves are read out only when no game is running; the saved data on the console is not changed (the app works on a copy of the image and deletes it afterwards).

Importing on the other console. Under “Import saved data” you choose the ZIP file on your computer (from this app or from Garlic SaveMgr). The app reads it through and shows title, files and size without changing anything; then you choose the user of this console. If that user already has saved data of this title, the app backs it up to the chosen drive first. The console makes a new image with its own formatter, the app writes the files into it (the account and user of this console go into param.sfo), reads every file back and compares it with the ZIP file. Only then does the image go to its place, with the picture of the saved data and the entry in the saved-data database (which is copied first); if anything fails, everything goes back to the state before. Then start the game and check the saved data. Saved data in the newer image format (fs_ext not 0: system blocks behind the data blocks) is created as a classic image from its data blocks (SYSTEM_BLOCKS 0, a little larger if needed); whether the game accepts it only shows when the game is started, and the app says so beforehand. Other image formats of newer firmware (for example param.sfo only in the image header) cannot be created by the app yet; it then says why. The owner details in param.sfo (the field PARAMS: the user ID and a value that is the same in all saved data of a user) cannot be made up by the app, for PS5 and PS4 alike: it takes them from another saved data of the same user on this console (first the same title and slot, then the same title, then any, last one of the other kind: PS4 for PS5 and the other way round). If there is none, the saved data is imported anyway, and the app says that the game may not accept it.

Safety checks. Shortly before the point of no return the app checks once more whether a game was started in the meantime, and then changes nothing. Apps (for example YouTube) are never imported, and their saved data is not used as a template for the owner details either. ZIP files with folder entries (for example from 7-Zip) are accepted. The copy of the saved-data database carries the date, time and saved data in its name. If a title has more than 16 saved data, the app reads nothing out and says so, so that none go missing unnoticed. The ZIP file holds no account ID in param.sfo (it is zero there); the other owner details stay in it because the import needs them: pass it on only to people you trust. An interrupted import (power loss, the app replaced, a crash) is finished or taken back by the next start of the app. The app tidies up: of the copies of the saved-data database the 10 newest of each user stay, and uploaded ZIP files that nobody imported within a day are removed. While a saved data is mounted, the fan control keeps working.

PS4 saved data works the same way, with three differences: the ZIP file holds the files only (no chives.json; Garlic SaveMgr writes none for PS4 either). When importing, the console makes a new key for the new image, which goes into the file <slot>.bin beside the image, and the size of the image is calculated from the files.

All saved data of a game. You do not need to know which saved data a game keeps (SaveData, sce_sdmemory …): “As ZIP” reads out every one, a ZIP file for each, all with the same time in the name. When putting in, you choose them together (browser: several files at once; fullscreen app: “put in all … saved data”); the app puts each into the place the ZIP file names and backs up the state before once for the whole game.

Fullscreen app: The same works with the controller, with a USB drive as the way: in the menu of a game (Square button) “ZIP auslesen auf …” (read out as ZIP to …) writes the ZIP file into the folder PS5-Sicherung/Spielstand-ZIP of the chosen drive (the target is the same as for the backups). On the other console the list “ZIP-Dateien” shows everything in that folder on the drives; the X button looks at a file (nothing is written), then “Für <user> einspielen” (put in for the user). The file on the drive stays. Its name may only hold letters, digits, “_”, “-” and “.”.

{{FIG:06-spiele-spielstaende.png}}

chapters.title: Packages
chapters.html:
Finds .pkg files on USB drives, disks and in console storage (on drives in the main folder and in the folder pkg, in console storage only in /data/pkg) and shows the picture, name, title ID, version, type and size.

  • Install… – the console installs the package itself; the app provides it and shows the progress. The installation begins with the click; if the console refuses the package, a plan opens below it that shows what is in the way.
  • Add to queue – puts packages into a list that is installed one after the other (each with the console’s normal installation). “Add all packages of this title” lines up the game, its updates and add-ons in the right order. A package the console refuses (already installed, game missing) is skipped with the reason; a failure halts the queue (“Continue”, “Retry”). The queue only lasts while the app is running.
  • Split… – splits large packages into parts for FAT32 sticks (up to 4 GB per file) or discs; the original stays unchanged.
  • Install from the PC – choose a .pkg on the computer running the browser, or drag it onto the card; it is sent in pieces while the installation runs and is not stored on the console. The page must stay open meanwhile.
An aborted installation attempt can leave space reserved. You free it again on the console, in the download list, with “Delete”.
{{FIG:07-spiele-pakete.png}}

chapters.title: Disc in the drive
chapters.html:
The Disc tab on the Games page shows which disc is in the drive and, on request, makes an image (ISO) of a PS2 DVD or a PS3 disc. It is based on ps-disc-detect (GPL-3.0), whose approach the app has rewritten.

If the console has no drive (a Digital Edition, a Pro without an attached drive), there is no “Disc” tab. The app checks whether one is there even with the watching off, without sending the drive any command.

  • Switch on: only when the switch is on does the app ask the drive (every second and a half). It stays on across a restart of the app.
  • Detection: the card shows the kind of disc (PS2 DVD-ROM, PS3 BD-ROM, PS4 BD-ROM, PS5 BD-ROM …) and its title ID, such as SLES-52780. PS4 and PS5 discs are only recognised, not copied. A console without a drive (Digital Edition) reports “no drive found”. The PS5's drive cannot read PS1 and PS2 CDs.
  • Create image: for a PS2 DVD or PS3 disc the button writes an ISO to /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/disc/, with progress, speed and time left. CRC-32, MD5 and SHA-1 are then shown with the image. “Cancel” deletes the unfinished file. While it runs, detection stays on and the console does not go into rest mode by itself. An image that is already there (also one made by ps-disc-detect in /data) is not read again.
  • Copy new discs automatically: the second switch makes the image right away when such a disc is inserted (off by default).
  • Redump: if /data/redump.db is on the console, the image gets its name from the list (when the title ID has exactly one) and is compared with the checksums (“checked against Redump”); otherwise it is named like the title ID. Build the list on a PC with tools/build_redump_db.py from the ps-disc-detect project (it downloads the files from redump.info); it may be up to 64 MB.
  • Delete an image with “Delete” or in the file manager.

Dumping disc games: “Start dumping” dumps right away

In the tab Disc, “Dump disc games” lists every game installed from disc. “Start dumping” (that is what the button is called as long as nothing speaks against it; otherwise it is called “Start”) starts the game and dumps it by itself after the load time (the dump queue with one title; the load time is in the queue settings, default 30 s). The app does not have to be opened again, because the game is in front of it. The console says “Dump started”, “Dump finished” or “Dump failed”. Requirements: the disc is in the drive, a target is chosen in the dump settings, no other game runs, the game has no dump yet, and no queue runs or is prepared; otherwise “Start” only starts the game and “Dump” follows by hand.

chapters.title: Files – the file manager
chapters.html:
Looking at the console's folders and downloading files works everywhere. Changing – uploading, new folder, renaming, copying, moving, deleting – also works everywhere, including system folders such as /user and the app's own folder. “View only” is left only for / itself, /mnt, /dev, /proc and links; the folders directly under / and under /mnt (for example /user, /data, /mnt/usb0) cannot themselves be renamed, moved or deleted, but their contents can. Areas the console has mounted read-only (e.g. /system) refuse a change by themselves; the app then reports the error.

/system_data and /user hold the console's databases and settings. Deleting or moving the wrong thing there risks a console that no longer starts or has to be set up again. Deleting asks first: a window names what will go (the names, file or folder, for folders the number of files and the size); only “Delete” in the window deletes for good, “Cancel” leaves everything as it was.
{{FIG:15-dateien.png}}

Sorting, selecting, viewing

  • Sorting: Above the list you choose “Name”, “Size” or “Date”; the arrow next to it reverses the direction. Folders are always at the top. The browser remembers the choice.
  • Select all: The box above the list selects all entries of the folder (except links and special files). Half filled means: only some of them are selected.
  • Folder sizes: “Calculate size” in the ⋯ menu of a folder counts how much is inside; “Folder sizes” does this for all folders in the view, one after another. A very large folder is reported with “at least” after about 8 seconds.
  • Viewing: “View” shows pictures (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, BMP, ICO) and the beginning of text files (up to 256 KB). Other files can only be downloaded.
  • Editing: For text files up to 64 KB “Edit” opens an editor; “Save” writes the file back. Download larger files, edit them and upload them again.

Copying & moving

  1. Tick entries (or open the ⋯ menu of a single entry).
  2. Press Copy to or Move to.
  3. In the destination picker choose a drive or a place of the console at the top, go into the subfolders and press Copy here or Move here.
  4. If a name already exists in the destination, a window asks: Replace, Keep both (the new entry is called “Name (2)”), Skip or Cancel. Replace writes a file next to the old one first and swaps it in at the end; a folder is merged.
  5. The display says how many files/folders there are and which one is being worked on (“Copying 1 of 2 files/folders”), from where to where (“from /mnt/usb0/new to /mnt/ext1”), percent, amount of data and the current file, plus the transfer rate (“82 MB/s”) and the estimated time left (“approx. 12 min left”). Cancel removes the entry that was started in the destination again.

Instead of “… to” you can use the clipboard: Copy or Cut, go to the destination folder and press Paste here. The fullscreen app works this way too.

Deleting

Delete asks first: the window says what will go – the names with kind and size, the folder, and for folders how many files with how much space are inside. Only Delete in the window deletes for good; Cancel (it has the focus) leaves everything as it was.

Uploading

Upload picks one or more files, Upload folder a whole folder (the folder structure is created, then the files go one by one); on a PC you can also drag either onto the list. A bar shows the progress per file. If the name already exists in the destination, the same window as for copying asks.

Protected: links are never followed, a mounted drive cannot be deleted as a whole, and copying and deleting never cross over to another drive. An entry cannot replace itself, and a file cannot replace a folder (or the other way round).

Drives are named as on the console: usb0, usb1 … – the folder /mnt/usb0 is “usb0”.

Eject a USB drive safely: next to every USB drive in the row of locations there is an Eject button (in the full-screen app: the Square button on the drive under “Locations”, or △ → More → Eject safely inside a folder of the drive). In the browser, the page then switches to System → Storage and ejects there, like the button there; in the full-screen app, the page no longer queries the drive. It is the same eject as under System → Storage: through ShadowMountPlus (1.7beta10 or later), only while no job of the app is running, PS4Mount plays no game from the drive and the app itself no longer has anything open on it; whether another program (such as an FTP server) has files open on it, the app checks only where the console allows it (not on the PS5 Pro with firmware 12.00), and then names that program. This is because the console detaches a drive by force and asks nobody. Before that, the app waits until nothing of it reads from the drive any more, and writes everything to the drive (sync). Unplug the drive only once the console says “… is ejected and can be unplugged”; simply pulling out a drive that is in use can damage its file system. While “Ejecting …” is still shown (two to seven seconds, depending on the drive), do not unplug it yet. If the console or the app crashed during the last eject, ejecting stays blocked until you allow it again on the “Files” or “System” page.

NTFS drives (Windows)

The console cannot mount drives formatted with NTFS, the file system of Windows. The file manager reads and writes them anyway, with a driver of its own: while the file manager is open, a plugged-in NTFS stick or NTFS hard drive appears under the locations after a few seconds as ntfs0, followed by “NTFS” and the drive’s name; a second one is ntfs1, and so on. Every NTFS partition of a drive (MBR or GPT) becomes a location of its own. A drive the console has already mounted something from (an exFAT partition, for example) is left alone by the app.

  • Works: opening folders, viewing and downloading files, Upload and Upload folder, New folder, Copy to and Move to in both directions (between the NTFS drive and the console, other drives or a second NTFS drive) and Delete – which asks first, as everywhere. The Windows folders “System Volume Information” and “$RECYCLE.BIN” are shown but cannot be deleted.
  • Does not work: Rename, Edit and replacing – the driver never changes existing files. If a name already exists in the target, the window offers only Keep both, Skip and Cancel. Names Windows does not allow (characters such as : * ? " < > |, a dot or space at the end, CON, NUL …) are written with _ in that place.
  • Games: since the console does not see the drive, games on it can neither be started nor mounted. Copy them to the internal storage or an exFAT drive first.

Read-only: if “Read-only” and a reason appear above the list (in the full-screen app as a note on the right), the app changes nothing on the drive. Usually Windows has not fully let go of the drive: it was unplugged without “Safely remove”, or Windows still has something open (Fast Startup, an unfinished chkdsk check). A drive that was unplugged from the PS5 in the middle of writing is read-only as well until a Windows PC has checked it. The note says what to do on the Windows PC; then plug the drive back into the PS5. Reading and downloading work either way.

Ejecting an NTFS drive: NTFS drives also have the Eject button in the row of locations (in the full-screen app: the Square button on the drive under “Locations”, or △ → More → Eject safely inside a folder of the drive). It needs no ShadowMountPlus and happens at once: the app writes everything pending to the drive, lets go of it and reports “ntfs0 can be unplugged now.” If the app is using the drive right then (copying, downloading, a listing), it says so and does not eject. An ejected drive only comes back when you unplug it and plug it in again.

Writing to NTFS is done by the app’s driver, not by the console. Back up important data on the drive first, and never unplug an NTFS drive while the app is writing to it – use “Eject” first. If writing fails, the app lets go of the drive and asks you to check it with chkdsk on a Windows PC.

The NTFS driver comes from PS5-NTFS-BROWSER by abcde6543 (GPL-3.0-or-later).

chapters.title: Payloads
chapters.html:
See and quit running payloads, and start saved ones with one click – from /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/payloads or from the USB stick (root or folder payloads). They are started via the console's payload loader (port 9021).

Profiles: A profile is a named sequence of payloads and pauses that “Run” starts step by step. One can be set as the startup profile; the app then runs it by itself after every start (with protection against endless loops). New payloads can be loaded into the console’s folder with “Import from PC”, also while editing a profile. “Back up profiles” and “Load profiles” exchange profiles as a file.

Download payloads: the same list as in itsPLK's Payload Manager (updated every day, currently 34 payloads) plus the payloads of strongt1me (ps5-payload-source), with search and categories. “Load list” fetches it once from GitHub; after that it is refreshed at most every three hours when the page is opened. “Download” puts the file into the payload folder, but only after its SHA-256 checksum matches the list. If the list has a newer version, the card shows “old → new” and “Update”. “Delete” only removes what the app downloaded itself; a foreign file of the same name is replaced only after the app has asked and named it (in the fullscreen app with a second press).

{{FIG:09-payloads.png}}

Files ending in .elf and .bin (etaHEN) count as payloads; both can be started and used in profiles, with the same check of the content.

chapters.title: Profile
chapters.html:
Change the display name of your account (at most 16 characters) and choose a profile picture – one of the 30 built-in ones or your own. Name and picture appear on the home screen after switching users; “Restore previous” brings back the picture before.

  • Web interface: choose your own picture on the phone or PC, “Crop” or “Fit”, then “Apply profile picture”.
  • Fullscreen app: put your own pictures (JPG or PNG up to 16 MB) into the folder /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/Profilbilder – the app creates it at start – or on a USB stick, in the root or in a folder Profilbilder. They appear first in the grid, marked “EIGENES”. The cross button applies a picture, the square button brings back the previous one, the triangle button changes the name.

Further down on the page (in the fullscreen app the “Account” view, L2/R2):

  • Activate offline account: you choose an existing user of the console; the app sets the account ID, type “np” and flags (like OffAct); the name stays as it is. Needs an active jailbreak.
  • Write fake sign-in and Reset fake sign-in: the first sends np-fake-signin to the payload loader (port 9021); it writes auth.dat, config.dat and registry entries. Resetting deletes only these files and entries and leaves the offline account untouched.
  • Back up and transfer profiles (web interface only): export “Web profile” (the settings of this browser) and “Game profiles” (the target temperatures per game) as a file and import them again on another device.
{{FIG:10-profil.png}}

chapters.title: System & log
chapters.html:
System shows the console, firmware, uptime, the storage of all drives, network, display and the cooling performance over the weeks.

  • Serial number (since 21.11.2026): The “Serial number” row on the System page shows only the last four characters by default (••••8023). The Full button in the row shows the whole number, Shortened switches back; in the fullscreen app the X button on the row switches. The choice is saved on the console and applies to the browser and the fullscreen app. The app has no login: while the whole number is switched on, every device on the home network can read it, which is why it is shortened by default.
  • Eject a USB drive (since 29.10.2026): Under “Storage”, every USB drive (/mnt/usb0 to usb7, /mnt/ext0) has an Eject button; in the full-screen app it is the X button under System → Storage. Ejecting is done through ShadowMountPlus (1.7beta10 or later), but only when no job of the app is running (copying, converting, moving, deleting, file manager, saves, installing or splitting packages, AMPR index, disc image), PS4Mount is not playing any games from this drive and the app itself has nothing open on the drive (it checks other programs only where the console allows it: not on the PS5 Pro with firmware 12.00). Otherwise the app does not eject and tells you what is still running. Why so careful: The console detaches the drive with a forced unmount and asks nobody whether anything on it is still open (this is so in every firmware from 3.20 to 12.70); whatever is still reading from the drive then gets dragged down with it. That is why, before ejecting, the app waits until nothing of it reads from the drive any more (Locations, Storage, Library, package and payload search), writes everything to the drive (sync), checks which files on the drive are open (those of the app itself always, those of other programs only where the console allows it; GET /api/v1/storage/holders?mount=/mnt/usb0 shows it), and writes a status report to the log shortly beforehand. Afterwards the console reports “… has been ejected and can be unplugged” or the reason why ShadowMountPlus refused (for example a game running from this drive). Important: The Eject button on ShadowMountPlus’s own page does not know about this app’s jobs and cannot be stopped by it; while a job is running, eject only through this app. In the file manager the page first switches to System → Storage (so that nothing on the file manager page queries the drive any more) and ejects there. Ejecting only detaches the drive by software: the console picks up some drives again by itself after a few seconds and mounts them anew, others only after they are plugged in again, so unplug the drive once it says “ejected”. Blocked after a crash: Shortly before ejecting, the app writes a marker and deletes it 30 seconds after the end. If it finds the marker at the next start, the console or the app crashed during the eject; ejecting then stays blocked (no button, and a notice with “Allow ejecting again” under “Storage” and on the “Files” page) so that this does not happen again. Safer: switch the console off completely and unplug the drive only afterwards.

System also shows a QR code with this page’s address: point the phone’s camera at it and the page opens on the phone (on the same network).

Right at the top of System is the ShadowMountPlus card (in the fullscreen app under System → ShadowMountPlus): there you set whether the version before or from 1.7beta12 runs (the new config.ini; the default is “Detect automatically”), and you switch ShadowMountPlus's “Update fakelib automatically” on or off.

{{FIG:11-system.png}}

Log lists every measurement, control action and message of the app (exportable). The Live kernel log tab shows the console's log as it is written – with filter, pause, save, download and recording. The app log is also written to /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/app.log (above 1 MB the old file becomes app.old.log), so it survives a restart or crash of the console; every start of the app begins there with a line ===== … gestartet =====. When the app ends the regular way (switching off or restarting through the app, being ended by the system, a crash), it writes a line ===== … beendet: <reason> =====; if that line is missing, the next start says so in a line of its own.

{{FIG:14-kernel-log-live.png}}

chapters.title: Credits
chapters.html:
The page thanks the developers whose work is in the app, and other well-known developers of the community – with profile picture, name and links. The links can only be clicked if the browser has internet access.

{{FIG:16-credits.png}}

chapters.title: Security on the home network
chapters.html:
• The interface has no login: every device on the home network can read and change things.
  • The console does not belong on the open internet – do not set up port forwarding to port 8086.
  • If you only want to use it on the device itself, enter 127.0.0.1 under Cooling → “Advanced settings” at “Bind address”.
  • The app refuses requests that recognisably come from outside websites (error 403). Since 21 November 2026 it only accepts requests via the console's IP address, localhost or a name with a home-network ending (.local, .lan, .home, .home.arpa, .internal, .localdomain, .intranet); a name such as ps5.fritz.box gets error 403 – then use the IP address.
  • ShadowMountPlus accepts requests from the whole home network by default since 1.7beta8 (port 10101, also without a login). If you don't want that, set api_bind_address=127.0.0.1 in its config.ini; the app talks to ShadowMountPlus over 127.0.0.1 anyway.
  • Kraken Mount (port 8097, only if you switched it on in the FPKGMount tab) and Dump Forge (port 8095, only during a conversion) are programs by other authors that the app starts. They listen on the whole home network and check neither Host nor Origin; the bind address and the protection against foreign websites do not apply to them. If you do not want that, leave Kraken Mount switched off.

chapters.title: If something does not work
chapters.html:
ProblemSolution
Web interface not reachableSend the ELF again (port 9021); only one instance; check the address http://<PS5-IP>:8086/.
Port 8086 in useA newly sent ELF ends an older instance itself. If that does not work (a very old version), end the old one on the “Payloads” page or restart the console.
Fan “not available”kstuff is not loaded – load kstuff, then send the app again.
“The drive has disconnected”Usually the USB cable: try a different, short cable directly on the console; afterwards restart the console if needed.
Tile opens nothingThe tile (FAKE86921 or FAKE86922) starts the app itself; after a restart the ELF no longer has to be sent. If it opens nothing: is its folder in /data/homebrew, and is ShadowMountPlus running (it creates the tile)? If need be, send the ELF once (port 9021).
Error 403 in the browserOpen the page directly via the console's IP address, not via another name or another website.

More answers are in the FAQ.

Page not reachable after a network change? When Wi-Fi is switched off and on or the cable is pulled, the console sometimes ends the web interface's access although the app keeps running (and so does the fan control). The app checks this every ten seconds, reopens the access by itself and says so in the log (“web interface … reopened”). After a few seconds the page loads again; the ELF does not have to be sent again.

items.q: What does the app actually do?
items.a: It controls the PS5's fan according to a target temperature – calm and slow rather than loud and hectic – and offers a web interface for games, packages, saved data, files, payloads, profile and system information.

items.q: Do I need internet?
items.a: No. The app only connects to programs on the console and to the browsers on your home network. The only exception, in the browser: the “Credits” page checks once whether github.com is reachable, so that the links become clickable. The console needs internet only when you trigger it yourself: “Load list” under “Download payloads” fetches the payload lists from GitHub (itsPLK and strongt1me), then “Download” fetches the single file; plus “Check for a new AMPR EMU NG version and load it” (the “APR-EMU version” window of a game) and “Download newer version from GitHub” (Dump Forge in the convert window, and FPKGMount). Only after the first “Load list” does the page renew the payload list by itself when it is opened, at most every three hours.

items.q: Which firmware is supported?
items.a: Firmware 12.00 on a PS5 Pro (CFI-7021) is tested; users report that the app also runs on 4.xx to 10.xx and on 13.60. The app is built with an SDK whose start-up code knows firmware 1.00 to 14.22; on the other versions the app has not been tested.

items.q: What has to run on the console for the app to work?
items.a: A PS5 with a jailbreak and a loaded ELF loader (elfldr, port 9021). For fan control kstuff must also be loaded; without kstuff the display and the web interface run, and the control reports “not available”. ShadowMountPlus is optional, but is needed for the tiles on the home screen, mounting and unmounting games, moving, unpacking and ejecting USB drives (mounting, unmounting and ejecting from ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta10). A browser on the home network is enough to operate it.

items.q: Does the app cost anything?
items.a: No. It is free software under the GNU GPL, version 3 or later.

items.q: Do I have to send the app again after every restart?
items.a: Not if you use a tile: FAKE86921 and FAKE86922 start the app themselves. Without a tile, yes – the ELF runs in memory and has to be sent to port 9021 once after every restart. The settings are kept.

items.q: The tile only opens an empty page – why?
items.a: This concerns the former media tile (PSCC69690): it did not start the app. Use the tile FAKE86922 (browser) or FAKE86921 (fullscreen); both start the app themselves.

items.q: Which tile do I need: FAKE86921 or FAKE86922?
items.a: FAKE86921 is the fullscreen app: it shows the app on the TV and is operated with the controller, with no browser at all. FAKE86922 starts the app just the same and opens the web interface in the console's browser. Both bring the app with them and start it themselves if it is not running yet; you can have both side by side. The folders from the zip files belong in /data/homebrew/, and ShadowMountPlus creates the tiles.

items.q: I copied new tile folders, but the app still shows the old version – why?
items.a: Up to 1.77.0 the tiles only sent their app when none was running, so an older app that was still running simply stayed. Since 1.77.1 a tile replaces an older running app when you tap it. An equal or newer one stays, and if a job is running (packing, copying, installing …) the tile leaves the app alone – open it again after the job. If the tiles on your console are still from 1.77.0 or older, send the new ELF once to port 9021 (it ends the old instance itself) or restart the console.

items.q: When I open the tile after a game, “Device busy” appears – what to do?
items.a: Usually just tap the tile again. So that it does not happen in the first place, the app pauses a game in the background itself as soon as the home screen is in front (switch Pause the game in the background below the operating mode on the Cooling page, on by default; in the fullscreen app under Settings). If the console refuses the start anyway, the app reports “Please be patient for a moment” and starts the tile once more itself. If the message stays with a game that you only mounted but never started, the Unmount button on the Games page helps.

items.q: How do I open the interface on a phone or PC?
items.a: Open http://<PS5-IP>:8086/ in the browser. The IP is in the notification on the TV after the start.

items.q: Can I start the app twice?
items.a: Usually it sorts itself out: if you send the ELF a second time or a tile starts a newer app, the new instance ends the older one itself. If that fails (a very old build; the console reports “Port 8086 is held by an older instance of this app”), you end the old one on the “Payloads” page (Already loaded payloads → “Quit”) or restart the console. Two instances at the same time both control the fan and interfere with each other.

items.q: How do I see the temperature without opening the page?
items.a: Press the controller's mute button twice quickly: the temperature and fan speed appear at the top left (without a sound).

items.q: Why doesn't the page move when a window is open?
items.a: That is on purpose: while a window is open, the background stays still, and the right stick only scrolls the window itself.

items.q: In which languages is the interface available?
items.a: German, English, Italian, Spanish, French, Russian and Swedish. You choose the language at the top right of the header (in the fullscreen app: Options button → “Sprache / Language”); the manual and the FAQ are available in all seven. Notifications that the console shows on the TV stay in German.

items.q: A text is still in German – is that a bug?
items.a: Not a bug in the app, but a gap: rare texts and console messages are not translated into every language and then appear in German. Please report them; the dictionaries are easy to extend.

items.q: How do I open the sidebar in the fullscreen app?
items.a: With the touchpad button. Left on the d-pad belongs to the page (e.g. the grid of profile pictures); L1 and R1 switch directly to the previous or next area.

items.q: How do I operate the fullscreen app with the controller?
items.a: Touchpad button: sidebar. L1/R1: previous and next area, L2/R2: the sub-tabs. D-pad: select and change values. X button: start or confirm, Circle button: back. Square button: actions for the selection, Triangle button: details or “More”. Options button: menu with “Open web interface in the browser”, “Reload”, “Sprache / Language”, “Quit app” and the power options. The bar at the bottom always shows what the buttons do right now. “Quit app” closes only the fullscreen app; the app on the console, and with it the fan control, keeps running.

items.q: Where do I put my own profile pictures for the fullscreen app?
items.a: In /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/Profilbilder or on a USB stick (root or folder Profilbilder), as JPG or PNG up to 16 MB. After a few seconds they appear first on the Profile page, marked “EIGENES”.

items.q: Why is my USB stick called “usb0”?
items.a: That is what the console itself calls it (/mnt/usb0). So the app counts from 0 as well: usb0, usb1 …

items.q: Why does the app show only part of my serial number?
items.a: By default the app shows only the last four characters (••••8023): it has no login, and the whole number could otherwise be read by every device on the home network. To see it in full, press Full in the “Serial number” row on the System page (fullscreen app: the X button on the row); Shortened switches back. The choice is saved on the console and applies to the browser and the fullscreen app.

items.q: Which target temperature makes sense?
items.a: 66 °C by default. Cool = 62 °C, Balanced = 77 °C, Quiet = 91 °C. Higher means quieter and warmer; up to 72 °C is a good range for most people. 91 °C is the value the console sets itself: as quiet as without the app, but the console gets noticeably warmer; the warning threshold moves with it automatically (target + 2 °C).

items.q: How do I make the fan even quieter?
items.a: On the Cooling page there are three places: raise the Target (the “Quiet” quick select sets 91 °C), choose the Operating mode “Quiet” (recommended; it does not change the target, only how strongly the fan responds to heat) and lower the Fan speed ceiling (30 to 100 %, 100 % by default). The ceiling does not apply above the emergency limit or in the fan guard. If you only want it quieter at night, switch on Night mode: between two times, a night target that is usually warmer applies. Quieter always means warmer too.

items.q: Can the app overheat my console?
items.a: The app only holds the temperature you set. Above the safety limit, all consideration for noise is dropped and the fan goes quickly to full speed; the PS5's firmware always protects itself independently of that. On top of that the fan guard watches: if the regulation hangs or it still gets too hot, it sets full cooling or hands the fan back to the console.

items.q: The console shows “Temperaturwarnung” – what does that mean?
items.a: The app warns when the processor reaches the “Warning from” threshold (80 °C by default, 5 °C more for the main chip): with a notification on the screen, and above the safety limit with a window. With a high target this would happen all the time, so in automatic mode the threshold rises with the target (switch “Warning threshold follows the target” in the advanced settings, on by default, never lower than target + 2 °C). If the warning comes anyway, make sure there is free ventilation (dust, distance from the wall) or lower the target; “Warning from” can also be raised.

items.q: Why doesn't the fan spin up immediately?
items.a: The control is deliberately slow: it works with an average, lets the speed rise gently from about 10 °C below the target and adjusts in small steps.

items.q: What happens when I quit the app?
items.a: Then the console controls the fan itself again according to its normal settings. The same applies when “Automatic mode” is switched off.

items.q: The fan is “not available” – what can I do?
items.a: kstuff is not loaded. Without kstuff, the app cannot reach the fan controller. Load kstuff and send the app again.

items.q: Does deleting a game delete my saved data?
items.a: No. Saved data is always kept when a game is deleted. Nothing is deleted until you confirm “Delete” in the window; the app never deletes a running game.

items.q: Which format should I choose when converting?
items.a: ffpfsc is compressed and recommended. ffpkg and exFAT are uncompressed. FPKG (a debug .pkg that Dump Forge writes) you only need for Kraken Mount (tab “FPKGMount”). Please recreate older .ffpkg files made with versions before 1.48.0. For exFAT and ffpkg the game can additionally be packed into LZ4 or zstd packs on the way (chapter “Games”).

items.q: Is the original deleted when I convert, copy or unpack a game?
items.a: No, by default it stays (“Original afterwards”: Keep). In the window you can choose Delete instead (the app asks first and names the name, size and path; saved data stays) or Move (first a checked copy into a folder of your choice, then the original is deleted). The original is deleted or moved only after the job has ended well; if it fails or you cancel it, the original stays untouched. Purpose: the same title should not lie on the console twice, otherwise ShadowMountPlus reports it from two places (chapter “Games”).

items.q: The window says “Unsigned executables” – what does that mean?
items.a: The game's executables (eboot.bin, .prx, .sprx) are plain ELF files, and the console does not start such files. When converting, and when packing into a new folder, the app writes them as FSELF (fake-signed); the game folder stays as it is. Packing in the game folder itself leaves them unchanged; with LZ4 you can choose the copy as a new folder next to it, zstd always packs in the game folder and replaces them there with FSELF versions as long as you leave the switch “Sign executables as FSELF” on.

items.q: A large package does not fit on my FAT32 stick.
items.a: FAT32 allows at most 4 GB per file. Under “Packages”, “Split…” cuts a package into suitable parts – the original stays unchanged.

items.q: An installation was aborted – where is my storage space?
items.a: The console reserves the space immediately. Remove the aborted entry from the console's download list with “Delete”.

items.q: Where are my saved data backups?
items.a: On the drive you choose when backing up, in the folder PS5-Sicherung/Spielstaende/<Datum> – on the internal SSD under /data.

items.q: Can I restore saved data from another console?
items.a: Not a backup made by the app: it is tied to its console and can only be verified there. To switch consoles, the “Saved data” page has the section “Transfer to another console”: press “As ZIP” at the title (PS5 and PS4), choose the ZIP file on the other console under “Import saved data” and pick the user (chapter “Back up saved data”). The ZIP file is not encrypted.

items.q: My game does not start after LZ4 packing. What now?
items.a: Tap “Unpack LZ4 …”: all files come back, checked byte for byte. Then test the game unpacked first with the same APR-EMU version. If it does not run like that either, it does not tolerate this APR-EMU. In detail in the chapter “LZ4 asset packs: step by step”.

items.q: LZ4 or zstd: which should I choose?
items.a: LZ4 is read by drakmor's APR-EMU (0.4.2.1 test-pack) and by AMPR EMU NG too; the app packs only the game data and leaves programs, media and delicate files loose (profiles, “Automatic”). zstd is read only by AMPR EMU NG, packs the whole game except the system files and usually saves more space. If a game runs with LZ4, there is no reason to switch. Both can be unpacked again with one click; to switch, unpack first.

items.q: Can I pack a game into LZ4 or zstd packs while converting it?
items.a: Yes, for exFAT and ffpkg of a PS5 game folder: choose the group “Packing (AMPR packs)” in the convert window. Dump Forge writes the image and packs on the fly; the original stays unchanged, and the source is read twice, so it takes longer. zstd works only with AMPR EMU NG, which Dump Forge puts into the game itself. The choice is greyed out for PS4 games and for games that already lie in packs. Details in the chapter “Games”.

items.q: Can the app copy discs?
items.a: A PS2 DVD or PS3 disc, yes: the Disc tab on the Games page, “Create image” makes an ISO with CRC-32, MD5 and SHA-1. PS4 and PS5 discs are only recognised. The PS5's drive cannot read PS1 and PS2 CDs.

items.q: Can I back up (dump) a game that is installed from disc as a folder?
items.a: Yes, in the Disc tab under “Dump disc games”: it lists the PS5 and PS4 games that are installed from disc. Choose a target under “Settings” → “Location”, insert the disc and press Start dumping on the game: the app starts the game and dumps it by itself after the load time (the game keeps running meanwhile). Several games one after another are handled by the “Dump queue”. Only for backups of your own games (chapter “Disc in the drive”).

items.q: I only use the ELF – do I need Dump Forge separately for the “FPKG” format?
items.a: Not necessary at all: since 21 November 2026 Dump Forge 0.5.7 is inside the app's ELF (packed; the ELF is about 8 MiB bigger because of it) and is unpacked in memory for every job; nothing is written to the console. This also applies to packing while converting to exFAT or ffpkg. A newer version you fetch in the convert window with “Download newer version from GitHub” (only on a button press) or put there yourself: copy the file ps5-dump-forge-VERSION-ps5.elf (the version only digits and dots, newer than 0.5.7) to /data/PS5-Cooling-Center/dumpforge/, for example by FTP; the highest version wins. The app makes the folder at every start.

items.q: My PS4 games from USB or my FPKG games do not show up – why?
items.a: “PS4 PKG from USB” (PS4Mount) and “FPKGMount” (Kraken Mount) have been switched off by default since 21 November 2026. Open the tab on the Games page and turn on the switch Switch on at the top; the app remembers the choice (on as well as off) and then starts both by itself every time it starts. After an update, if you had never switched it on, you have to switch it on once. The games then appear with their icon on the home screen.

items.q: Why can't I change some folders?
items.a: Since 1.75.3 everywhere, including system folders such as /user or /user/download and the app's own folder. Only / itself, /dev, /proc, mounted drives as a whole, the folders directly under / and /mnt themselves (for example /data, /user, /mnt/usb0; their contents stay changeable), folders under which something is mounted, and links are locked; what the console has mounted read-only it refuses by itself. Take care under /system_data and /user: they hold the console's databases and settings.

items.q: May I change anything in the app's folder?
items.a: Yes, since 1.75.3 the app's folder (/data/PS5-Cooling-Center) can be changed too. Caution: the app's settings and logs are stored there; change only what you know.

items.q: Is anything overwritten when copying?
items.a: Only if you want it. If a name already exists in the destination, a window asks: “Replace”, “Keep both” (the new entry is called “Name (2)”), “Skip” or “Cancel”. Replace writes a file next to the old one first and swaps it in at the end; a folder is merged. Copying games on the Games page, by contrast, never overwrites.

items.q: What happens with “Cancel”?
items.a: The operation stops; whatever of the started entry had already been written to the destination is removed again.

items.q: How do I view a file without downloading it?
items.a: With “View” on the file: pictures (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, BMP, ICO) appear in a window; for text files, the beginning up to 256 KB. Binary files can only be downloaded.

items.q: Can I edit a text file directly on the console?
items.a: Yes: for text files up to 64 KB (for example .txt, .ini, .json, .toml), Edit in the ⋯ menu of the file opens an editor; “Save” writes the file back. This only works where the file is writable; otherwise the window only shows the text. Download larger files, edit them and upload them again.

items.q: Can I sort the list by size or date?
items.a: Yes: above the list you choose “Name”, “Size” or “Date”; the arrow reverses the order. With “Folder sizes”, the console also counts the size of the folders.

items.q: How do I eject a USB stick safely – and why is it back afterwards?
items.a: In the file manager, next to every USB drive in the row of locations there is an Eject button (in the fullscreen app: the Square button on the drive under “Locations”); the same eject exists under System → Storage. It runs through ShadowMountPlus (from 1.7beta10) and works only when no job of the app is running, PS4Mount plays no games from the drive and the app itself no longer has anything open on it (it checks other programs where the console allows it). The console detaches a drive by force and asks nobody; that is why the app first waits until nothing of it reads from the drive any more. Unplug the stick only when the console says “… is ejected and can be unplugged”. While “Ejecting …” is still shown (two to seven seconds, depending on the drive), do not unplug it yet. The console only detaches it by software: it picks up some drives again by itself after a few seconds, others only after they are plugged in again. If the console crashed during the last eject, ejecting stays blocked until you allow it again; safer then: switch the console off completely, then unplug.

items.q: Can the app read and write Windows NTFS drives?
items.a: Yes, in the file manager – even though the console itself does not mount NTFS. The drive appears under the locations as ntfs0. Uploading, new folders, copying, moving and deleting work; renaming, editing and replacing do not, and games cannot be started from it. If it says “Read-only”, Windows has not fully let go of the drive; the note says what to do on the PC. A stick that was unplugged in the middle of writing is read-only as well until a Windows PC has checked it. Press “Eject” before unplugging it.

items.q: “The drive has disconnected (Device not configured)”
items.a: Almost always the USB cable, the port or too little power. Try a different, short cable directly on the console; if there are problems afterwards, restart the console.

items.q: I get error 403.
items.a: The app refuses requests that come from outside websites, and since 21 November 2026 also addresses with a name that does not have a home-network ending such as .local, .lan or .home (for example ps5.fritz.box). Open the interface directly via the console's IP address.

items.q: Is the interface password-protected?
items.a: No. Every device on the home network can use it. So do not set up port forwarding; if you like, set the “Bind address” under Cooling → “Advanced settings” to 127.0.0.1 (“Local only”). ShadowMountPlus (port 10101) and, as long as they are running, Kraken Mount (port 8097, off by default) and Dump Forge (port 8095, only during a conversion) also accept requests from the whole home network without a login; the app's bind address does not apply to them. You restrict ShadowMountPlus in its config.ini with api_bind_address=127.0.0.1; leave Kraken Mount switched off.

items.q: Unknown folders with zip files in /data/homebrew?
items.a: They usually come from another tool with automatic saved data backup (e.g. ProsperoMgr), not from this app.

items.q: Backing up, restoring or “As ZIP” does not work because a game is running – what to do?
items.a: Saved data is only touched when no game is running – not even a paused one: a game waiting in the background can still hold the saved data open. Close the game (Close game on its card) and try again. This applies to backing up, restoring, “Delete” of saved data, “As ZIP” and “Import saved data”.

items.q: Is this legal?
items.a: The app contains no games, no firmware, no foreign keys (only a publicly known one for self-built test packages) and nothing that circumvents copy protection. Modifying a console may violate terms of use; whoever does it bears the risk. Piracy is not supported.

items.q: The page stutters when scrolling in the PS5 browser.
items.a: Since 1.71.2 the background of the “Standard” design is a single colour, and the regular refreshes pause briefly while you scroll. If that is not enough, choose the “Optimal” design (the fastest to draw).

items.q: After a game the console shows an error message (“Device busy”) when I tap the tile – what to do?
items.a: Since 1.86.5 the app pauses a game in the background itself as soon as the home screen is in front (Cooling → “Pause the game in the background”, on by default). The tile then starts without a failed first start and without a message. If the switch is off, or you tap within the first second after the PS button, the app starts the tile once more by itself after a few seconds.

items.q: After using “Mount” on a game, no other game and no tile starts any more (“Device busy”) – why?
items.a: ShadowMountPlus has only one place for a mounted game that has not been started yet; as long as it is taken, it refuses every other start, and the console shows a launch error. Start the mounted game or press Unmount on it (the Games page shows a yellow notice for this; in the fullscreen app the row carries the mark MOUNTED). The app also releases a game it mounted itself and nobody started, on its own: at once when it starts another game itself or the console refuses another start (then simply try the start again), otherwise after 30 seconds.
